- **Your own link back to a row** — "back to the list" after a detail page — is a push navigation, and the browser scrolls to the top when it has finished: a `scrollIntoView()` from a `$watch` on `routeName` is undone. Give the row an `id` and navigate to its fragment: `this.navigateUrl = "/#photo-" + id` (or `attr.to: backHref`). The browser scrolls to the row and focus moves to it (a link, a button, an element with `tabindex`); `scroll-margin-top` clears a sticky header.


---

# Reference: I/O node catalog + signals quick reference

<!-- source: wcstack-skill/skills/wcstack-app/references/io-node-catalog.md -->

# wcstack I/O Node Catalog + signals Quick Reference

Sources: each package's README (ja preferred) plus the `static wcBindable` / `static observedAttributes` declarations in src, `packages/signals/README.ja.md`, `docs/signals-definition-timing.md`, `docs/architecture-hardening/12-wc-bindable-observable-inventory.md`, `docs/audio-tag-design.md`, `docs/midi-tag-design.md`, `docs/timing-and-firing-contract.md`, and `examples/signals-live-search`. Tag surface verified at v4.28.0: **53 tags**, attribute spellings, properties, commands and the timing notes below source-verified. **4.0 changes no I/O node tag, property or command.** Two things an author sees: every package's `bootstrapXxx(config)` **throws** on an option it does not have, a value of another type, an unknown `tagNames` key or a non-string tag name (`[@wcstack/fetch] bootstrapFetch: "tagName" is not one of its options, or not of the option's type.` — `/auto` passes none, so a CDN page is unaffected), and `@wcstack/state` 4.0 delegates `on*:` handlers of bubbling events to the root (`state-binding.md` §8) — I/O-node wiring through property / `command.` / `eventToken.` / spread bindings is unchanged.

History, for reading older pages: `mountNode` and the normative headless Cores arrived in 1.23, observation semantics (§0) in 1.24, `@wcstack/audio` / `@wcstack/midi` in 1.25, scoped-registry support in 1.31, `<wcs-view-transition>` in 1.32, `<wcs-media-query>` in 2.2; no tag, property or command name has changed since it was added. Two wiring shapes needed a minimum `@wcstack/state` on 3.x — the dotted property form (`.once:`) and `class.` / `attr.` / `style.` on a wc-bindable tag from 3.3, I/O nodes inside `for:` rows from 3.4 — and all of them work in 4.0.

## 0. Common Conventions (all I/O nodes)

- **One-line CDN**: `<script type="module" src="https://esm.run/@wcstack/<pkg>/auto"></script>` alongside `@wcstack/state/auto`. **Load every I/O node (and `@wcstack/devtools/auto`) BEFORE `state/auto`** — module scripts run in document order, so this guarantees the elements are defined before state binds. Property/spread bindings survive a late definition (deferred via `whenDefined`, applied with the latest value — in `for:` / `if:` rows too), but a **command-token emit is never replayed** — an emit inside the undefined window is silently dropped. Where the order is out of your hands (autoloader, embedded snippet), gate the emitting control with `<wcs-defined timeout>` on its `pending` output, never with an `await customElements.whenDefined()` inside the handler (that promise never rejects → permanent hang on a failed load).
- **Pre-upgrade property writes are adopted**: assigning an input on a not-yet-defined element (`el.url = "…"`) creates an own data property; every Shell calls `upgradeProperties(this)` first thing in `connectedCallback`, re-running the declared `wcBindable.inputs` through their setters. Declared inputs only, and the command-token asymmetry above is unchanged.
- **wc-bindable**: each tag declares via `static wcBindable` its **properties** (observable outputs; state subscribes) / **inputs** (write surface; the optional `attribute` is the kebab-case markup name) / **commands** (invocable methods). State writes an input's **property only**; each tag reflects its own attributes in its setters (a boolean flag as a present / absent attribute), so `active: isPlaying` on `<wcs-wakelock>` holds the lock only while `isPlaying` is true, and `keepAlive: recording`, `watch:`, `manual:` follow `false` too. (3.x also wrote the attribute itself, as `"false"`, which those inputs read as true.)
- **`null` and `undefined` on an input** (wc-bindable 0.10's producer guidance): `null` clears an attribute-backed input — the attribute goes and the documented default applies, so a boolean that is **on by default** (`<wcs-audio>` `limiter` / `resumeOnGesture`, `<wcs-debounce>` `trailing`, `<wcs-throttle>` `leading`) goes back **on**, not off; `undefined` restores what the markup said. Neither becomes the string `"null"` / `"undefined"`. State never writes `undefined` (write-skip), so in a state app only `null` matters: to switch a default-on flag off, bind `false`, never `null`. Momentary inputs (`trigger`, `notice`, `say`, `send`) ignore both; `<wcs-storage>`'s `value = null` removes the stored key.
- **Observation semantics**: every observable property declares `semantics: "state" | "event" | "handle"`. `state` is a *current value* — the same-value guard applies, so writing an `Object.is`-equal primitive skips the set, the dependency walk, the DOM apply and `$renderedCallback`. **`event` properties are occurrences and bypass that guard**: the same `message` arriving twice updates state twice. The occurrence outputs, worth knowing because they are the ones where repetition carries meaning:

  | tag | occurrence outputs |
  |---|---|
  | `<wcs-ws>` / `<wcs-sse>` / `<wcs-broadcast>` / `<wcs-worker>` | `message` |
  | `<wcs-clipboard>` | `text` `items` `copied` `cut` `pasted` |
  | `<wcs-notify>` | `clicked` `closed` `shown` |
  | `<wcs-speak>` | `charIndex` `spokenWord` |
  | `<wcs-listen>` | `result` |
  | `<wcs-debounce>` / `<wcs-throttle>` | `fired` |
  | `<wcs-recorder>` | `recorded` `dataavailable` |
  | `<wcs-camera>` | `ended` |
  | `<wcs-midi>` | `message` `type` `channel` `note` `velocity` `control` `value` — all seven are derived getters over the one `wcs-midi:message` occurrence |
  | `<wcs-audio>` / `<wcs-analyser>` | `noteOn` `noteOff` / `frame` |

  Everything else — including `error` / `errorInfo` / `loading` / `value` / `trigger` — is `state`. The single `handle` is still `<wcs-camera>`'s `streamReady` (a live `MediaStream`): never route it through state, wire it element-to-element (§2) — since 4.5 the lint warns `wcs/handle-bound-as-value` on `streamReady: <path>`. **`@wcstack/audio` adds zero handles** despite owning a live `AudioNode` graph — the graph is a descriptor, not a value, and the Core owns and disposes it (ADR-14 G2), so the 10 new outputs audio + midi contribute are all `event`.
- **Wiring**: output binding `data-wcs="value: users"` / command-token `data-wcs="command.<method>: $command.<name>"` / event-token `data-wcs="eventToken.<property>: <name>"` / spread `data-wcs="...: slot"`.
- **Since 4.5 (the `state-field-report` seam app)**:
  - **A disconnect publishes every state output it changes** (`timing-and-firing-contract.md` §22): `loading: false`, `<wcs-camera>` `active: false`, `<wcs-recorder>` `recording: false`, `<wcs-speak>` `speaking: false`, `<wcs-listen>` `listening: false`, `<wcs-ws>` `connected: false`, a cleared `error`. The router puts a left route's nodes back with their bindings, so I/O nodes inside route content now come back right; before 4.5 a camera looked on and a spinner never ended.
  - **A feature this page cannot use is `"unsupported"`**: on an insecure origin, under a `Permissions-Policy` that turns it off, or in an `<iframe>` without `allow="camera; microphone; geolocation"`, `<wcs-permission>` and the acquirer's `permission` (`<wcs-camera>`, `<wcs-geo>`, `<wcs-listen>`, `<wcs-notify>`) say `unsupported`, the browser is not asked, and `errorInfo` is `capability-missing` with the reason. Branch on `unsupported` for "not available on this page" and on `denied` for "allow it in the site settings" — Chromium's own Permissions API says `granted` / `denied` in those cases.
  - **Refused commands warn** (`[wcs/command-not-ready]` — once per outage since 4.8, once per element before): a `<wcs-upload>` `trigger` / `upload()` with no files or no `url`, a `<wcs-fetch>` `trigger` with no `url`, a `notify()` without the permission, and since 4.6 a `<wcs-storage>` load / save / remove without a key. Since 4.6 also `[wcs/post-uncloneable]` (a `<wcs-worker>` / `<wcs-broadcast>` post structured clone cannot copy), `[wcs/input-as-attribute]` (an object written as an attribute: `files="[object File]"`) and `[wcs/fetch-helper-undefined]` (an undefined `<wcs-fetch-header>` / `<wcs-fetch-body>`: a page that defines the tags itself defines `WcsFetchHeader` / `WcsFetchBody` too, or loads `/auto`). Also `[wcs/storage-unserializable]` (a `Blob` / `File` / `Map` / `Set` in a saved value), `[wcs/speech-echo]` (speaking while a `<wcs-listen>` listens) and `[wcs/camera-keep-alive-missing]` (the tab hidden while recording without `keepAlive`).
- **Since 4.8 (the `shift-desk` seam app — a page left open for a shift)**:
  - **Connect-time work waits one microtask** (`timing-and-firing-contract.md` §23): whether to connect / load / start / observe, and with which inputs, is decided in a microtask after `connectedCallback`, with the inputs as they are then. The router puts a route's same nodes back on a parameter-only navigation before state writes the next route's inputs, so up to 4.7 a route's `<wcs-ws data-wcs="url: chatUrl">` joined the previous ticket's chat first (and `<wcs-camera>` the previous device, `<wcs-permission>` the previous permission). `<wcs-storage>` / `<wcs-broadcast>` / `<wcs-worker>` still load / open / start at once on their first connect. A stop command in the same task as the append (`close()`, `stop()`, `release()`, …) leaves the element stopped; reading `readyState` / `running` right after appending sees the start one microtask later — await one in tests.
  - **`stale-after="<ms>"` on `<wcs-sse>` / `<wcs-ws>`** for pages that stay open: a connection that died without being closed (a laptop's sleep, a NAT, a proxy) stays `OPEN` and `connected: true` forever otherwise. With it, nothing received for that long → `connected: false`, `error` says why, sse reopens the same `url`, ws reconnects under `auto-reconnect`. The server must send something the element receives more often than that (an SSE comment line or a WS ping frame does not count).
  - **`<wcs-ws>` closes on a persisted `pagehide` and reconnects on `pageshow`**, so a page with a socket is restored from the back/forward cache instead of reloaded; what arrived meanwhile is not replayed — resync when `connected` turns `true`.
  - **`[wcs/command-not-ready]` once per outage** (again after the element was ready in between), and `<wcs-idle>`'s `start()` without the permission says it too.
  - **A page that stays open needs its own wake handler** — `$connectedCallback` does not run on wake, resume, a bfcache restore or a visibility change; `<wcs-timer>` ticks are not time (throttled when hidden, lost asleep — read `Date.now()` on each tick); `<wcs-raf>`'s `dt` is active time. Recipe: `docs/long-lived-pages.md` (one handler for `visibilitychange` / persisted `pageshow` / `resume` / `online` / a clock gap; notifications summarized after a wake; bounded lists; a key per record for drafts).
- **Common idioms**:
  - `manual` attribute = do not auto-start on connect. **No `manual` does NOT imply auto-start**: idle / tilt / accelerometer / gyroscope / magnetometer / ambient-light-sensor never auto-start — they are inert until the `start` command.
  - `trigger` is a **momentary input property**, not a command (`command.trigger` exists only on `<wcs-debounce>` / `<wcs-throttle>`, which have no trigger property). **No edge detection**: any truthy write fires, then self-resets to `false`, and it bypasses `manual` — a state slot seeded `true` fires at bind. Always seed trigger slots with `false`.
  - **Frozen-after-connect**: most inputs are read at connect or at the next command call only — changing the attribute later is silently ignored. Live (reacting to change): fetch/ws/sse `url`, storage `key`, broadcast `name`, worker `src`, camera constraint attrs, intersect/resize target + geometry, wakelock `active`/`type`, timer `interval` (while running only), media-query `query` (re-subscribes, generation-guarded so a stale list can never write). Frozen surprises: permission `name`, defined `tags`, sensor `frequency`, idle `threshold`, clipboard `monitor`, notify `mode`, listen options while listening, recorder options while recording.
  - **Never-throw**: failures land in the `error` output; nothing throws. Too-early writes are dropped, not queued — ws `send` before connected, broadcast `post` before `open`, worker `post` before `start`, a recorder `start` with no stream all divert to `error` — and since 4.3 the element also warns `[wcs/command-not-ready]` (once per outage since 4.8; the message is lost either way). Bind `error` in every app.
  - fullscreen / pip / pointer-lock `target`: re-resolved at each command invocation; default is the first child element, else the element itself.
  - Event names are `<tag-name>:<kind>` (exceptions: screen-orientation uses `wcs-orientation:*`, `<wcs-throttle>` uses `wcs-throttle:*`).
  - Nearly every node has `error` / `errorInfo` outputs (the ones without: timer / raf / debounce / permission / network / media-query / intersection / resize). Sensor-family `error` is sticky — a later successful `start` does not clear it. Omitted from the table.

## 1. Catalog

| package | tag | key attributes / inputs | properties (outputs) | commands |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **fetch** | `<wcs-fetch>` (helpers: `<wcs-fetch-header name value>` `<wcs-fetch-body type>` `<wcs-infinite-scroll>`) | `url`(live: change re-fetches — in-flight aborted. The auto-fetch guard remembers the last url **actually fetched**: writing it again is skipped (`"a"→"a"`); since 4.3 an empty url in between forgets it, so `"a"→""→"a"` fetches again (up to 4.2 it was skipped); re-running the same url needs an explicit trigger. Since 4.3 a url change that sends a non-GET with no body warns `[wcs/fetch-auto-unsafe]`, and a change aborted by a newer request on the same element warns `[wcs/fetch-request-superseded]`) `method` `target` `manual` `body`(one-shot: consumed per fetch; a mid-flight write stages for the NEXT fetch; a retry needs it written again — the same string is no change for a binding, so write a new object each time: `[wcs/fetch-body-gone]` warns since 4.23) `response-type`(auto/json/text/blob/arrayBuffer) `trigger`(no-op while `url` is empty) | `value` `loading` `error` `status` `objectURL` `trigger` | `fetch` `abort` |
| **storage** | `<wcs-storage>` | `key` `storage-key` (`storageKey`; `key` under a name React and Vue leave alone, since 4.6 — `key` wins when both are written) `type`(local/session) `value` `manual` `trigger` | `value` `loading` `error` `trigger` (with cross-tab sync) | `load` `save` `remove` (all synchronous) |
| **upload** | `<wcs-upload>` (helper: `<wcs-upload-header name value>`, 4.9) | `url` `method` `field-name` `multiple` `max-size` `accept` `manual` `files`(auto-upload fires on `files` write — since 4.6 files that came before `url` wait for it and go when it arrives, so JSX `files={files} url=…` uploads; another `url` change does not upload; **used up by every upload** — success, failure or abort set it back to `null`, like fetch's `body` — so assign the files again before a retry; in one `data-wcs` write `trigger` after `url` and `files`, since bindings apply in the order written) `trigger` | `value` `loading` `progress` `error` `status` `files` `trigger` | `upload` `abort` |
| **websocket** | `<wcs-ws>` | `url` `protocols` `auto-reconnect` `reconnect-interval` `max-reconnects` `binary-type` `stale-after` (4.8) `manual` `trigger` `send` (writing a value sends immediately; objects are auto-JSON-serialized). Options besides `url` are read per `connect`; clearing `url` does not disconnect — `close` does | `message` `connected` `loading` `readyState` `trigger` `send` | `connect` `sendMessage` `close` |
| **sse** | `<wcs-sse>` | `url` `with-credentials` `events` `raw` `stale-after` (4.8) `auto-reconnect` `reconnect-interval` `max-reconnects` (4.9) `manual` `trigger`. Options besides `url` apply only via `close`→`connect` (`connect` to the same url is a no-op) | `message` (`{ event, data, lastEventId }` — `data` is **already parsed** when the payload is JSON (do not `JSON.parse` it again; set `raw` to get the string); a named event arrives only when listed in `events="a,b"`) `connected` `loading` `readyState` `trigger` | `connect` `close` (receive-only) |
| **broadcast** | `<wcs-broadcast>` | `name`(live: change reopens the channel) `manual` | `message` (no self-echo; structured clone) | `open` `post` `close` |
| **worker** | `<wcs-worker>` | `src` `type` `name` `manual` `keep-alive`(thread outlives disconnect — caller must `terminate` or it leaks) `restart-on-error` `max-restarts`(cumulative lifetime budget) `restart-interval` | `message` `running` | `start`(no-op while the same `src` runs — `terminate`→`start` to apply option changes) `post` `terminate` |
| **timer** | `<wcs-timer>` | `interval`(default 1000; live while running only — frozen while stopped/paused) `once` `repeat` `immediate` (all read at `start`) `manual` `trigger` | `tick`(counter) `elapsed`(ms) `running` `trigger` | `start` `stop` `reset` `pause` `resume` (`stop`→`start` continues `tick`/`elapsed` — only `reset` zeroes) |
| **raf** | `<wcs-raf>` | `once` `repeat` (read at `start`) `manual` `trigger` `reduced-motion`(`"run"`(default)/`"pause"` — with `"pause"`, frame delivery stops while `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` holds and resumes with a `dt = 0` boundary; opt-in because a tick is functional output, not decoration) | `tick` `elapsed` `dt` `running` `suspended`(two causes: hidden tab, or the engaged reduced-motion gate — counters freeze, `running` stays true) `trigger` — `elapsed` counts active time only, not wall-clock | `start` `stop` `reset` `pause` `resume` (`stop`→`start` continues counters — only `reset` zeroes; `pause` is user intent, the reduced-motion gate is environment — `resume` never overrides the OS preference) |
| **debounce** | `<wcs-debounce>` / `<wcs-throttle>` (`wcs-throttle:*` events) | `source` (value-surface input; NO same-value guard — every write restarts the wait, and the initial bind write starts a cycle: throttle emits `value` immediately at startup) `wait` `max-wait` `leading`(debounce: opt-in attr, default off; throttle: default on, opt-out `no-leading`) `trailing`(default on; opt-out `no-trailing` — a bare `trailing` attribute is inert) | `value`(settled value; `null` until the first settles) `fired` `pending` | `trigger` `cancel` `flush` (commands — no momentary trigger property here) |
| **clipboard** | `<wcs-clipboard>` | `monitor` | `text` `items` `loading` `readPermission` `writePermission` `monitoring` `copied` `cut` (both carry the document selection text, not the clipboard payload) `pasted` | `writeText` `write` `readText` `read` `startMonitor` `stopMonitor` (write requires a user gesture) |
| **geolocation** | `<wcs-geo>` | `high-accuracy` `timeout` `maximum-age` `watch` `manual` `trigger` (attributes are read at connect time) | `position` `latitude` `longitude` `accuracy` `coords` `timestamp` `watching` `loading` `permission` | `getCurrentPosition` `watchPosition` `clearWatch` |
| **permission** | `<wcs-permission>` | `name` (one tag, one permission) `user-visible-only` `sysex` | `state`(granted/denied/prompt/unsupported) `granted` `denied` `prompt` `unsupported` `unsupportedReason` (4.25: why it is `unsupported` — `policy-blocked` = the page it is embedded in forbids it, `insecure-context`, `no-permissions-api`, `unknown-name` = the browser cannot say; `null` otherwise) | none (monitor-only) |
| **notification** | `<wcs-notify>` | `notice` (reactive display; guarded vs the LAST SHOWN text — first non-empty bind fires; the `notify` command bypasses the guard) `mode`(auto/constructor/sw) `body` `icon` `badge` `tag` `lang` `dir` `require-interaction` `silent` `renotify` `manual`(mutes reactive `notice`; `notify` still works) | `permission` `granted` `denied` `prompt` `unsupported` `clicked` `closed` `shown` | `request` `notify(title, options)` `close` `closeAll` — without `granted`, `notice`/`notify` silently no-op into `error`: call `request` first (for SW use, `wireNotificationClicks()` from `@wcstack/notification/sw`) |
| **intersection** | `<wcs-intersect>` | `target` (default = first child / selector / `self`; non-matching selector → silent no-op, `observing` false) `root` `root-margin` `threshold` (live — but ALL attribute changes are ignored while `manual`) `once` `manual` `trigger`(re-runs `observe`) | `entry` `intersecting` `ratio` `visible` (latched on first intersection) `observing` `trigger` | `observe` `reobserve` `unobserve` `disconnect` `reset` (after `once` fires the observer is disconnected — `reset` alone can't re-latch `visible`, use `reobserve`) |
| **resize** | `<wcs-resize>` | `target` `box` `round` (live — but ignored while `manual`; selector no-match = silent no-op) `once`(fires on the INITIAL size delivery = measure-once) `manual` `trigger`(re-runs `observe`) | `entry` `width` `height` `observing` `trigger` | `observe` `unobserve` `disconnect` |
| **wakelock** | `<wcs-wakelock>` | `active` (desired input — durable intent: a request while hidden waits and auto-re-acquires on return to visible) `type` `manual`(gates only the connect-time auto-acquire) | `held` (actual output; reflects OS release) | `request` `release` |
| **camera** | `<wcs-camera>` | `audio` `facing-mode` `device-id` `width` `height` (live: changing while active re-acquires with the new constraints) `autostart`(connect-time only) `keep-alive` | `active` `permission` `audioPermission` `deviceId` `devices` `streamReady` (raw MediaStream; RE-FIRES with a NEW stream on every re-acquire — switchCamera / constraint change / visibility resume — consumers must re-attach) `ended` | `start` `stop` `switchCamera` |
| **camera** | `<wcs-recorder>` | `mime-type` `timeslice` `audio-bits` `video-bits` (properties `audioBitsPerSecond`/`videoBitsPerSecond`; all read at `start`) | `recording` `paused` `duration` `mimeType` `blob` `objectURL` `recorded` `dataavailable` | `attachStream` `start` `stop` `pause` `resume` (`start` without an attached stream errors and warns `[wcs/command-not-ready]`; re-attaching mid-recording applies to the NEXT `start` only). Since 4.5 `mimeType` (and the `Blob`'s type) is the type recording started with even without `mime-type`; read it with `mimeType#init=element:` — a plain two-way `mimeType:` writes the state's seed into the request. Leaving the document mid-recording delivers what was recorded as `recorded` |
| **speech** | `<wcs-speak>` (TTS) | `say` (reactive speech; guarded vs the LAST SPOKEN text — first non-empty bind speaks) `rate` `pitch` `volume` `voice` `lang` `manual`(mutes reactive `say` — bind it to the listening flag to break the listen→speak echo loop) | `voices` `speaking` `paused` `pending` `charIndex` `spokenWord` `unsupported` | `speak` (imperative; fires even on same value) `cancel` `pause` `resume` |
| **speech** | `<wcs-listen>` (STT) | `lang` `continuous` `interim` `max-restarts`(`continuous` alone still ends at the first silence — set `max-restarts` > 0 to keep the session alive) `manual` `trigger` (options frozen while listening) | `interimTranscript` `finalTranscript` `result` `listening` `permission` `unsupported` `trigger` | `start` `stop` `abort` |
| **defined** | `<wcs-defined>` | `tags` `mode` `timeout` (timeout detects load failure; ALL inputs frozen at connect; empty `tags` → `error`, `defined` stays false) | `defined` `pending` `missing` `count` `total` `error` (invariant: total=count+pending+missing) | none (event-token only; monotonic; terminal) |
| **fullscreen** | `<wcs-fullscreen>` | `target` (a CSS selector — `"#viewer"`, not `"viewer"`; `"self"`; omitted = first child) | `active` (bind it; do not keep a flag of your own. 4.25: goes `false` when the element leaves the document — up to 4.24 it stayed `true`) `error` `errorInfo` `supported` (4.25: this page can use it — offer the button only then) — `false` on an iPhone | `requestFullscreen` `exitFullscreen` (need a tap; lock the orientation from a `$watch` on `active` — `references/device-apis.md` §5) |
| **picture-in-picture** | `<wcs-pip>` | `target` (must resolve to a `<video>` — otherwise `error`) | `active` (4.25: `false` when the element leaves the document) `error` `errorInfo` `supported` (4.25: this page can use it — offer the button only then) — `false` in Firefox | `requestPictureInPicture` `exitPictureInPicture` (need a tap; keep the video and its `<wcs-pip>` outside the router to play on across pages) |
| **pointer-lock** | `<wcs-pointer-lock>` | `target` | `active` (4.25: `false` when the element leaves the document) `error` (4.25: also set for a refusal Firefox reports as an event) `errorInfo` `supported` (4.25: this page can use it — offer the button only then) | `requestPointerLock` `exitPointerLock` (need a tap; the movement is read from `mousemove`'s `movementX` / `movementY` by the page) |
| **screen-orientation** | `<wcs-screen-orientation>` | (no inputs) | `type` `angle` `portrait` `landscape` (output-only: read when the binding attaches) `error` `errorInfo` `supported` (4.25: the orientation can be watched — it does not say a `lock` will hold) | `lock` (takes the orientation — emit from a state method, never `onclick: $command.lock`; holds only while the document is fullscreen; Safari has none) `unlock` |
| **idle** | `<wcs-idle>` | `threshold`(default 60000; read at `start` only) | `userState` `screenState` `active` (`false` before `start()` — show "away" from `userState === "idle"`, which is `null` until then) | `requestPermission`(needs a user gesture) `start` `stop` |
| **network** | `<wcs-network>` | (no inputs) | `effectiveType` `downlink` `rtt` `saveData` `supported` (Firefox/Safari: `supported` false, data fields `null` — bindings must handle null) `offline` (4.1: `!navigator.onLine` with the window events, every browser — `disabled: offline`; not `online`, because a name starting with `on` is an event binding) | none (monitor-only) |
| **media-query** | `<wcs-media-query>` | `query` (the one input, mirrored from the attribute; **live** — changing it while connected tears down the old `MediaQueryList` subscription and subscribes to the new one, generation-guarded; removing it = watch nothing → `matched` false; an invalid query does not throw — `media: "not all"`, `matched: false`). No secure-context or permission requirement | `matched` `media` `supported` — all `state`, all derived from one `wcs-media-query:change` snapshot, so a query change that flips `media` and `matched` together arrives as one update. `matched` is a strict boolean (never `null`; `false` whenever there is no live list), `media` the browser-normalized string (`""` with no list), `supported` = `typeof matchMedia === "function"` resolved per subscription (Node/SSR: `false`). **The output is `matched`, not `matches`** — `Element.prototype.matches()` exists on every element. `:state(matched)` / `:state(supported)` are reflected for CSS | none (monitor-only) |
| **share** | `<wcs-share>` | (no inputs) | `value` `loading` `cancelled` (`value` is written only on success — stale after a cancel/failure, check `cancelled`) `error` `errorInfo` `supported` (4.25: this page can use it — offer the button only then) | `share` (takes the data — emit from a state method, in the tap; invoking while `loading` is a silent no-op; `canShare(data)` is a method of the element, for files) |
| **contacts** | `<wcs-contacts>` | (no inputs) | `value` (an array of contacts whose members are arrays — `name: ["山田"]`; give it a slot of its own) `loading` `cancelled` (4.25: a picker closed without a choice — up to 4.24 that wrote `value: []` and `cancelled` never came) `error` `errorInfo` `supported` (4.25: this page can use it — offer the button only then) — Android Chrome, top-level pages only | `select` (takes the properties — emit from a state method, in the tap) |
| **credential** | `<wcs-credential>` | (no inputs) | `value` (carries the password — bind it only where that is meant) `loading` `cancelled` (user cancel surfaces as `NotAllowedError`, not `AbortError`) `error` `errorInfo` `supported` (4.25: this page can use it — offer the button only then) — password credentials: Chromium only (4.25: `capability-missing` elsewhere; it was `credential-failed`) | `get` `store` (they share one in-flight lane — a concurrent call supersedes and silently drops the first; 4.25: `store({ id, password })` builds the `PasswordCredential`; store only after the server accepted the pair) `preventSilentAccess` (4.25: on sign-out, or the next visit signs the user back in) |
| **eyedropper** | `<wcs-eyedropper>` | (no inputs) | `value` `loading` `cancelled` `error` `errorInfo` `supported` (4.25: this page can use it — offer the button only then) — Chromium on a desktop | `open` (a second `open` aborts the prior pick into `cancelled`) `abort` |
| **tilt** | `<wcs-tilt>` | (no inputs) | `alpha` `beta` `gamma` `absolute` (`alpha` is relative on both phone platforms — not a compass) `heading` (4.25: degrees clockwise from north, `null` until known) `permissionState` (`"denied"` = the user's answer; 4.25: a call that was not a tap leaves it as it was, with `errorInfo` `not-allowed`) `error` `errorInfo` `supported` (4.25; says nothing about a sensor being there) | `requestPermission` `start` `stop` (iOS: `start` before `requestPermission` is silently dead — no events, no error; emit both in one tap) |
| **accelerometer** | `<wcs-accelerometer>` | `frequency` (a positive number of Hz; 4.25: anything else warns `[wcs/frequency-invalid]` and means the default rate) | `x` `y` `z` (m/s², one event for the three — `eventToken.x`'s `event.detail` is `{ x, y, z }`) `permissionState` (4.25) `error` (sticky) `errorInfo` `supported` (4.25) | `start` `stop` `requestPermission` (4.25: the iPhone's motion question — where the browser has no `Accelerometer` class the element reads `devicemotion`; up to 4.24 it was `capability-missing` on an iPhone) |
| **gyroscope** | `<wcs-gyroscope>` | `frequency` | `x` `y` `z` (rad/s) `permissionState` (4.25) `error` (sticky) `errorInfo` `supported` (4.25) | `start` `stop` `requestPermission` (4.25; as accelerometer) |
| **magnetometer** | `<wcs-magnetometer>` | `frequency` | `x` `y` `z` `error` (sticky) `errorInfo` `supported` (4.25; `false` on an iPhone and wherever the class is behind a flag — no fallback) | `start` `stop` |
| **ambient-light-sensor** | `<wcs-ambient-light-sensor>` | `frequency` | `illuminance` `error` (sticky) `errorInfo` `supported` (4.25; rarely `true` — fall back to `prefers-color-scheme`) | `start` `stop` |
| **midi** | `<wcs-midi>` | `input`(omitted = every input port; else port id or case-insensitive name prefix) `output`(omitted = first output port) `channel`(1-16; omitted = all — system messages always pass) `sysex`(a separate, more restricted grant — leave off) `auto`(connect + request on connect). `input`/`output`/`channel` are live: they **re-hook the existing access**, never re-request, so no second permission prompt | `message` `type` `channel` `note` `velocity`(**normalized 0-1**) `control`(raw 0-127) `value`(raw 0-127, but **-1..1 for pitch bend**) `devices` `connected` `permission` `granted` `denied` `unsupported` `error` `errorInfo` | `request` `close` `send` |
| **audio** | `<wcs-audio>` — the patch root | `volume`(0-1, clamped since 4.17) `limiter`(on by default: compression from -18 dBFS and, since 4.17, a hard ceiling at -6 dBFS — up to 4.16 the README's own patch clipped at +5 dBFS; `limiter="off"` to measure real amplitudes) `resume-on-gesture`(default on; `"off"` = drive it yourself with `command.resume`). Bound from state as booleans (`limiter: on`), the setter writes `"on"` / `"off"` | `state`(running/suspended/unsupported) `running` `suspended` `unsupported` `voices` `noteOn` `noteOff` `warnings` `error` `errorInfo` | `resume` `suspend` `noteOn(note, velocity)` `noteOff(note)` `allNotesOff` |
| **audio** | node tags `<wcs-osc>`(`type` `frequency` `detune` `glide` `transpose`) `<wcs-noise>` `<wcs-biquad>`(`type` `frequency` `q` `gain` `detune`) `<wcs-gain>`(`gain`) `<wcs-delay>`(`time` `feedback` `mix`) `<wcs-shaper>`(`amount`) `<wcs-env>`(`attack` `decay` `sustain` `release` `depth`) `<wcs-lfo>`(`type` `rate` `depth`) | every numeric attribute above is a bindable input and is **live**; the routing attributes `id` / `out` / `param` / `note` / `master` and `<wcs-voice poly>` are **structural** (a change rebuilds the graph) and are deliberately NOT bindable | none — a node tag is a pure input surface (everything observable belongs to `<wcs-audio>`) | none |
| **audio** | `<wcs-analyser>` | `fft` `smoothing` (+ structural `master`) | `frame` (occurrence — `sample()` returns a **freshly allocated** array, so retaining a frame is safe) | `sample(mode)` — `"wave"` (default) or `"fft"`. It produces data only; drawing is your canvas's job |

Fetch / SSE notes (4.1): `<wcs-fetch-header name="Authorization" data-wcs="value: authHeader">` sets a header from state (a header with no `value` is not sent); a request that needs state (a token) also takes its `url` from state — a getter that is `null` until the token is there — because the I/O packages load first and a literal `url` fetches before state set the header. **One `<wcs-fetch>` is one request at a time** (a new one aborts the in-flight one; a still-`true` `trigger` drops a second `true`): give each overlapping mutation its own element. A `422`'s field errors arrive in `error.body` as text: `get fieldErrors() { try { return JSON.parse(this.saveError?.body ?? "{}").errors ?? {}; } catch { return {}; } }`. SSE: the browser sends `Last-Event-ID` only after an event with an `id:` — after loading a snapshot, put its position in the stream `url` (`?since=`) and **keep it fixed while the stream is open** (write it when you open or reopen on purpose, not on every event — a `url` that changes per event reopens the stream per event). A stream the browser gave up on (a 502 while the server restarts, a 401, a wrong content type) is never retried by the browser: since 4.9 `auto-reconnect` (with ws's `reconnect-interval` / `max-reconnects`) reopens it with the element's `url` at each attempt, so a token a getter put in the url is the fresh one; a reopen sends no `Last-Event-ID`, so skip events already applied by id. Clearing a stream's or socket's `url` closes it (a `url` getter that is `null` after sign-out ends the previous user's stream). `<wcs-sse>` closes itself when the page unloads and reopens when the document stays (a router navigation) — write no `beforeunload` listener of your own. By hand: reopen with `close()` + `trigger`, and tell it from `errorInfo.recoverable === false`, not `readyState === 2` (`readyState` is `CLOSED` before the first connect too, and a `$watch` fires once for the starting value). A token in the stream `url` is the one it opened with: a native reconnect after it expired gets a 401, which looks like a 502. Firefox logs `The connection … was interrupted while the page was loading.` on a full navigation with a stream open (a plain `EventSource` too) — harmless; closing it in a `beforeunload` listener avoids it.

Fetch results (4.9 docs): **`value` is the last response until the next one lands** — while a new `url` is in flight and after an empty one (a route left) — so a page that reads it as the item it shows checks that it is (`v && v.id === this.entryId`). **`value` and `status` fire nothing for the same value**: a `$watch` on `status` sees the first `DELETE` answered `204` and not the second. To act on every response take the response event — `eventToken.value: done` + `$on: { done(state, event) { … } }`, `event.detail` is `{ value, status, objectURL }`, dispatched for every response, an HTTP error included, before `loading` turns `false` — or watch `loading` going from `true` to `false` and read `error`.

Upload headers (4.9): `<wcs-upload-header name="Authorization" data-wcs="value: authHeader">` inside `<wcs-upload>` sends a header, read when an upload starts (up to 4.8 the element could send none — a token API needed `UploadCore`); a header without `value` is not sent; a `Content-Type` header drops the multipart boundary (warned). A page that defines the tags itself defines `<wcs-upload-header>` too (`[wcs/upload-helper-undefined]`).

### 1.1 `@wcstack/audio` is a graph, not a value (read before writing a patch)

The audio package does not follow the `manual` / `trigger` idioms above — it has a shape of its own:

- **Nesting is the signal chain.** A parent tag's output feeds each nested child; a leaf (no chain children, no `out`) reaches the master output. Anything nesting cannot express is routed by id: `out="bus"` (many-to-one), `out="vcf.frequency"` (drive any `AudioParam`), `param="frequency"` (modulator shorthand for the *parent's* parameter).
- **`<wcs-voice poly="8">` makes its subtree a template** — one fresh graph per held note, with release tails and oldest-note stealing. Outside a voice the graph is live and monophonic.
- **Structure is declared, values are reactive.** Numeric attribute/property writes apply live to every instance including sounding voices; structural attributes (`id` `out` `param` `note` `master` `poly`), and adding/removing/moving an audio tag, **rebuild — which cuts every sounding voice audibly**. Any other DOM change does nothing (a `<div>` added among your sliders must not silence the instrument). Rebuilds coalesce onto a microtask and an unchanged re-submit is free.
- **Writes are accepted synchronously; when they become *audible* is deliberately unspecified** (render quantum + output latency are hardware-dependent). Parameter changes are smoothed over ~20 ms as part of the contract, and the effective value is never read back — a getter returns what you last wrote. This is the cross-cutting rule for any node with an external clock.
- **Audio cannot start before a gesture.** `<wcs-audio>` resumes the shared context on the first click/keypress — since 4.17 it creates it there too (or at the first `resume()` / `noteOn()`), so the browser prints no autoplay warning on load; `state` reads `suspended` until then. Since 4.18 a gesture creates it once that gesture ends, after the click — 4.17.0 did it inside the `pointerdown`, and a hint bound to `running` that hid there moved the page under the pointer, so the page's first click landed elsewhere. The `AudioContext` is shared page-wide (browsers cap concurrent contexts); each root keeps its own master gain and limiter. `noteOn` reaches **every** `<wcs-voice>` of a root (they layer): two instruments are two `<wcs-audio>` roots.
- **Structure is declared, values are bound.** `type`, `mix` and the envelope times are live settings like the numeric params; a structural attribute (`id`, `out`, `param`, `note`, `master`, `poly`) or an audio tag added / removed (`if:` / `for:` around audio tags) rebuilds the graph and cuts every sounding voice — since 4.17 `<wcs-audio>` warns `[wcs/audio-voices-cut]` once when it does. A taken-out `<wcs-audio>` publishes `voices: 0` and `state: "suspended"` (4.17).
- **A voice patch with no `<wcs-env>`** gets an implicit 5 ms attack so it cannot click, and is released on note-off. Voices are reclaimed on the audio clock, never on a timer.
- **Headless**: `new AudioGraphCore()` + `setPatch({nodes:[…]})` takes the same descriptor as a plain object; pass your own `createContext` to render into an `OfflineAudioContext` (no gesture, faster than realtime, deterministic). SSR renders nothing and reports `unsupported`.

### 1.2 `<wcs-view-transition>` is a policy node, not an I/O node

`@wcstack/view-transition` renders nothing, binds no data, and describes no animation — it decides *whether* a DOM change animates and what a collision does; the animation stays in CSS (`::view-transition-*`). **Enter animations never need it** (`@starting-style` on the inserted element); it exists for **leave and move**, which CSS cannot reach (wcstack detaches removed nodes synchronously; a reorder has no intermediate state).

- **Inputs**: `for`(`router` / `state`, space-separated; default both) `mode`(`latest`(default: skip the running transition, animate the newcomer) / `queue` / `exhaust`(apply immediately, drop only the animation)) `naming`(`manual`(default: you bind `style.viewTransitionName`) / `auto`(state names every list row and `if` branch, with `view-transition-class` `wcs-row` / `wcs-branch` for group CSS)) `naming-limit`(default 200) `reduced-motion`(`skip`(default — honors `prefers-reduced-motion` by applying without animating) / `animate`) `types` `disabled`(bindable — a page can switch animation off from state). **Outputs**: `active` `error`. **Commands**: `skip()` (finish the running transition now; its DOM change still lands).
- **The rule everything is subordinate to: a DOM change is applied exactly once, whatever happens to its animation** — unsupported browser, hidden tab, a page not drawn yet (4.10.1 — an update before the first frame is applied at once; a test that counts transitions right after load waits for a frame first), reduced motion, `disabled`, collision, or a throwing `startViewTransition` all still end with the change applied.
- **One per document** (a second warns and stays inert). Requests in the same microtask join one transition (a route change and the state drain it triggers animate together).
- **Only a change of structure animates (4.1)** — a state update that adds / removes / moves list rows or switches an `if` branch runs in a transition; one that only updates values is applied at once (typing in a bound input never starts a transition — before 4.1 each keystroke did, and the page ignored clicks while it ran).
- **`for="state"` (on by default) makes a state update that changes structure land on a frame** instead of a microtask; since 4.10 `$watch` and the `$stream` restart wait for it, so the mechanism order stays bindings → `$renderedCallback` → `$watch` → `$stream` restart (up to 4.9 it flipped to `$watch` → `$stream` restart → `$renderedCallback` — `state-binding.md` §10). Code that writes state then reads the DOM after `await Promise.resolve()` must wait for the transition. `for="router"` keeps state timing untouched. Participation is per document, not per element.

### 1.3 `<wcs-fetch>`: what reports nothing

- **A command runs before the bindings of its own update.** A handler that writes `url` (or `body`) and emits `command.fetch:` in one go sends the request with the url and body from **before** the change — the list is one page behind, a post carries the previous body. Give the url to the command (`this.$command.load.emit("/api/items?page=" + n)`, `fetch(url, init)`), or write the inputs and fire with `trigger` — bindings apply in the order written: `data-wcs="body: payload; trigger: sending"` (`forms.md` §8). The order holds across elements too, and a `trigger` sends what the element and its `<wcs-fetch-header>` / `<wcs-fetch-body>` hold when it applies: in a logout, write the trigger before clearing the session its `Authorization` header reads — the other order sends no token, and the server keeps the session valid.
- **The end of a request is the response event, not a `$watch` on `status` / `value`.** The same value fires nothing — a second `DELETE` answered `204` never moves the page on. Bind `eventToken.value: done` + `$on` (`event.detail` is `{ value, status, objectURL }`, for every response, errors included — check `status`), or watch `loading` go from `true` to `false`.
- **`value` is the previous response until the next one lands**, also after an empty `url`: an edit form fills itself from the previous record. Check the response is for the item shown (`v && v.id === this.entryId`).
- **One `<wcs-fetch>` per request kind.** An element that loads by `url` and also posts by `method` + `body` + `trigger` sends a `POST` with no body on every later url change (the method stays; a body is sent once) — `[wcs/fetch-auto-unsafe]`.
- **An I/O element in a `for:` row that a reorder moves** goes on where the browser has `moveBefore()` (Chromium 133+, Firefox 144+); in Safari the move aborts the request without a word (`loading` false, `status` 0). Do not reorder while a row's request is in flight, or keep the I/O elements in a list that does not move.

## 2. Minimal state-integration examples for high-frequency nodes (from each README)

**fetch** — a computed URL drives the fetch (auto re-runs on url change; aborts any in-flight request):
```html
<wcs-fetch data-wcs="url: usersUrl; value: users; loading: listLoading; error: listError"></wcs-fetch>
<ul><template data-wcs="for: users"><li data-wcs="textContent: users.*.name"></li></template></ul>
```
On an HTTP error `value` goes back to `null` — bind `error` too, and put a getter in front of a fetched list (`catalog: null` + `get products() { return this.catalog ?? []; }`) so `for:`, row getters and handlers never see `null`. The lint cannot read the response, so a list that starts `null` has no row shape: declare it with JSDoc (`@wcstack/lint` 4.0.2+) or every row field is `wcs/binding-path-missing`:
```js
/** @typedef {{ id: number, name: string, price: number }} Product */
export default {
  /** @type {Product[] | null} */
  catalog: null,   // value: catalog — rows of `for: products` now have .id / .name / .price
```
Retry with `trigger:` (write `true`; the element resets it to `false` when done) — seed it `false` (`wcs/trigger-seeded-truthy`). A `body:` bound to an object is **one-shot**: `body` resets to `null` after each `fetch()`, and a write below the bound path (`newUser.name`) does not re-apply it, so a second submit sends no body (`wcs/input-nested-write` since 4.0.3) — assign a fresh body object in the submit handler, and bind `body:` to that slot (`submit() { this.submitBody = { name: this["form.name"] }; this.submitRequest = true; }`; a retry builds it again).

**storage** — two-way persistence. Bind `value` with **`#init=element`** so the persisted value wins the initial sync (without it the state's seed is written to the element first and saved over the stored value on every load — `wcs/storage-seed-clobber`), and seed the slot with **`null`**, which is what an empty key loads as (`#init=element` pulls it in, so a `""` / `[]` seed is gone on a first visit — `wcs/storage-init-seed`):
```html
<!-- state: username: null -->
<wcs-storage key="username" data-wcs="value#init=element: username"></wcs-storage>
<input data-wcs="value: username">
```
(Seeding `undefined` with a plain `value:` is the storage README's fallback only for a page that turns `$behavior.enableDirectionalInitialSync` off; with it on, the element's load event can fire before the binding exists.)
**Several inputs, one key (the storage README canonical form)**: give the state an **accessor pair** and bind it with `value#init=element` — `get formSnapshot() { return { name: this["form.name"], email: this["form.email"] }; }` / `set formSnapshot(v) { if (v) this.form = { ...this.form, ...v }; }` + `<wcs-storage key="signup-form" data-wcs="value#init=element: formSnapshot">`. On load the stored object goes through the setter once (`null` for an empty key, which then seeds it), typing a field dirties the getter and saves the new object, and the save's own `value` event — dispatched while state writes `value`, with the same object — is state's own write coming back, not a write (`state-binding.md` §6 has the rule; no `$behavior` key changes it). Another tab's save arrives as a new object and runs the setter; across tabs the key is one unit, the last save wins — so a draft that belongs to one window (a half-filled form) wants `type="session"`: it survives a reload and each tab keeps its own. A stored value also outlives a deploy, and a tab still open on the previous version receives what the new one saves: keep a version in the stored object and migrate in the setter, or change the key with the shape. JSON keeps no `Blob` / `File` / `Map` / `Set` (each is stored as `{}`): keep recorded clips and picked files out of the saved value (4.5 warns `[wcs/storage-unserializable]`). **Read the fields as `this["form.name"]`, never `this.form.name`** — the latter tracks `form` only, so editing never re-evaluates the getter (`state-binding.md` §6). The on-demand variant — `manual` + a getter of `$dependOn` calls bound to `trigger:` — remains for saving at a moment of your choosing.
**A list (a cart) is the same rule, one level down.** A binding is re-applied only when **its own path** is assigned, so `value: cart` misses every `this[`cart.${i}.quantity`] += 1` — the page shows 2, storage holds 1, nothing is logged (`wcs/input-nested-write`). Bind an accessor pair that reads each line by path through a row getter and `$getAll`; keep only what the user chose (ids, quantities) and look the rest up from the catalog with row getters, so a stored line never carries a stale price:
```js
get "cart.*.saved"() { return { id: this["cart.*.id"], quantity: this["cart.*.quantity"] }; },
get savedCart() { return this.$getAll("cart.*.saved", []); },
set savedCart(lines) { if (Array.isArray(lines)) this.cart = lines; },   // null on a first visit is ignored
// <wcs-storage key="cart" data-wcs="value#init=element: savedCart"></wcs-storage>
```
Forgetting `#init=element` on the accessor pair empties the stored cart on reload (the getter's `[]` is written first) — `wcs/storage-seed-clobber` reports it since 4.0.3. Changes saved by another tab arrive through the setter (the `storage` event), so two tabs share the cart with no extra code. A stored cart is restored **before** a fetched catalog arrives: write the lookup getters with `?.` / `??`.

**Saving when the page chooses** (a Save button for settings): give the element a slot the page assigns only then — `<wcs-storage key="settings" data-wcs="value#init=element: saved">` with `saved: null`, `save() { this.saved = { ...this.settings }; }`, and a `$watch` on `saved` that copies a loaded value into `settings`. Not `manual` + `trigger: settingsChanged` with a getter that returns `true`: the element writes `trigger` back (`[wcs/path-readonly]` on every change, lint error), and `manual` loads nothing, so the saved settings never come back.

**websocket** — receive via `message`; to send, just write a value to `send`:
```html
<wcs-ws url="wss://example.com/ws"
  data-wcs="message: lastMessage; connected: isConnected; send: outgoing"></wcs-ws>
<!-- state side: sendChat() { this.outgoing = { type: "chat", content: this.chatInput }; } -->
```

**timer** — declarative `setInterval` equivalent:
```html
<wcs-timer interval="1000" data-wcs="tick: count; running: isRunning"></wcs-timer>
<!-- one-shot: <wcs-timer interval="3000" once data-wcs="tick: showBanner"> — to bind `once` from state, write `.once: flag`; `once:` without the dot is an event binding -->
```

**media-query** — a media query as a boolean in state, for the cases where the answer has to reach *logic* rather than a stylesheet (a theme default, pausing a loop under `prefers-reduced-motion`, swapping a table for cards below a breakpoint, `(display-mode: standalone)` for a PWA); a styling-only query stays in CSS `@media`:
```html
<wcs-media-query query="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" data-wcs="matched: isDark"></wcs-media-query>
<main data-wcs="attr.data-theme: theme">…</main>   <!-- get theme() { return this.isDark ? "dark" : "light"; } -->

<wcs-media-query query="(max-width: 600px)" data-wcs="matched: narrow"></wcs-media-query>
<template data-wcs="if: narrow"><ul data-wcs="for: rows">…</ul></template>
<template data-wcs="if: narrow|not"><table>…</table></template>
```
One tag, one query — compose several elements for several queries. The first `wcs-media-query:change` fires synchronously during `connectedCallback`, before state has attached its listeners, and events are not replayed; the value still arrives because every output here is output-only, which makes the default binding authority `element` — the binding **reads the property when it attaches** (directional initial sync, on by default). Only in a state that declares `$behavior: { enableDirectionalInitialSync: false }` is a manual `$connectedCallback` pull needed. `matched` is never `null`, so `|not` is safe. Any node's commands can be driven from it, but for `<wcs-raf>` under `prefers-reduced-motion` prefer its own `reduced-motion="pause"` attribute.

**intersection** — lazy loading (`visible` is latched on first intersection; `once` disconnects):
```html
<wcs-intersect once data-wcs="visible: shown">
  <img data-wcs="src: src" alt="lazy">
</wcs-intersect>
<!-- infinite-scroll edge detection: <wcs-intersect target="self" data-wcs="intersecting: atEnd"> -->
```

**A list that loads its pages with `<wcs-fetch>`: use `<wcs-infinite-scroll>` (since 4.24).** A sentinel after the list (`wcs-infinite-scroll { display: block; min-height: 1px; }`) that runs a `manual` `<wcs-fetch>`: `<wcs-infinite-scroll target="page-fetch" root-margin="240px 0px" data-wcs="disabled: noMore">`. Write the target's `url` from state (`url: nextUrl`, never a static page-1 `url`), append and advance the page number in the `eventToken.value` handler on success only, set `noMore` on a short page. Since 4.24 it loads the first page when state writes the url, goes on while a page leaves it on screen (a tall window), never repeats a failed request, and stops at a response that added no row; up to 4.23 it missed all of these — on 4.23 use the `<wcs-intersect>` pattern below. When a filter changes, emit `command.abort:` first, then empty the list and reset the page: a `manual` `<wcs-fetch>` does not abort on a new `url`. `root` takes an id or a selector on both sentinel elements (4.24); write `root-margin` lengths with `px` or `%`. See `references/long-lists.md`.

**With `<wcs-intersect>` — a list that grows at both ends, or an edge the page schedules itself — paginate from the feed's length, not `page++`.** `<wcs-intersect>` reports that visibility *changed*; it cannot schedule, and it has no "qualified re-entry" event. `examples/state-intersect-scroll` is built around a `$stream` entry that owns the page fetch, and the shape it landed on is the one to copy:

- **Derive the requested page from what the feed already holds** — `page = floor(feed.items.length / pageSize) + 1`, written by the sentinel's `$on` handler — instead of incrementing on each edge. Under `$stream`' switchMap restart a blind `page++` is *wrong*: a second edge would abort page N in flight and jump to N+1, silently skipping a page. With the derived form, edges arriving while page N is active or failed write the same primitive, the same-value guard makes the enqueue a no-op, and the stream does not restart. That replaces the hand-written `if (loading) return` exhaust gate entirely. **Keep `page` a plain property**: a getter derived from `feed` and read by the stream's `args` would restart the stream on its own result and load every page with no sentinel.
- **The producer owns retry.** `$stream` is switchMap, not `retryWhen` — no automatic reconnection. Put a finite `1 + maxRetries` attempt loop and an abort-aware delay inside the async generator; final failure surfaces as `$streamStatus.<name> === "error"` + `$streamError.<name>`. Yield the success as `{ kind: "success", page, pageSize, items }` — `pageSize` rides on the success chunk so the fold needs only `feed` and the chunk.
- **"Run the same page again" is an occurrence, and the restart API is value-based** — encode it as a changing dependency (`retryNonce`) read by `args`. A Retry button increments it. This is a real boundary of the current API, not a workaround you can skip.
- **`reobserve()` only after a full page lands**, never on error — from a `$watch` on the feed (below): with the sentinel still visible, a new observer's first callback fires immediately, so error layout becomes an infinite retry scheduler. A partial page sets `feed.noMore` in the fold instead.
- **The feed is a plain key, folded by a `$watch` on the stream's value.** A stream's `fold` resets to `initial` on every restart, so it can only hold the current page; the value that outlives page runs is a key you seed and write (`state-binding.md` §15):

  ```javascript
  feed: { items: [], pages: [], noMore: false },
  $watch: {
    pageResult(chunk) {                          // fires on every landing; nothing has to be bound
      if (chunk?.kind !== "success") return;     // progress chunks and the restart's reset
      const feed = this.feed;
      if (feed.pages.includes(chunk.page)) return;   // page key
      this.feed = { items: feed.items.concat(chunk.items), pages: [...feed.pages, chunk.page],
                    noMore: chunk.items.length < chunk.pageSize };
    },
    feed(feed) { if (!feed.noMore) this.$command.rearm.emit(); },   // re-arm after a full page
  },
  ```

  Bind `for: feed.items` / `if: feed.noMore`. `feed` survives restarts and reconnects and needs nothing bound, so the visible meter stays display-only. **The page key is not optional**: the watch fires once per *landing*, not once per page, and a Retry after `done` (`retryNonce`) or a re-attached page lands the same page again. Commit-before-reobserve is the mechanism order — the `pageResult` watch writes `feed` in one batch, and the `feed` watch fires at the end of the next, after the new rows render (without a `<wcs-view-transition>` accepting `state`; with one, bindings apply on a frame and the watch runs first — `state-binding.md` §10). The status mirror (`get streamStatus() { return this["$streamStatus.pageResult"]; }` plus a `$watch` on it — a `$watch` key cannot start with `$`) remains only to record when an error settles, for the scroll-retry qualification. The demo in this form passes the same e2e suite on 3.4.0, 3.5 and the 4.0 engine. There is no `$scan` in 4.0: an older page's `$scan: { feed: { from: "pageResult", … } }` is exactly the `$watch` above (`state-binding.md` §16).

**clipboard** — copy via command-token (write requires a user gesture):
```html
<wcs-clipboard data-wcs="command.writeText: $command.copy"></wcs-clipboard>
<button data-wcs="onclick: onShare">Share</button>
<!-- state side: $commandTokens: ["copy"], onShare() { this.$command.copy.emit(this.message); } -->
```
Read with `command.readText: $command.paste; text: pasted`; monitor with the `monitor` attribute + `eventToken.pasted: ...`.

**notification** — command-token (display) and event-token (click) coexist on one tag:
```html
<wcs-notify data-wcs="
  command.request: $command.request;
  command.notify:  $command.notify;
  eventToken.clicked: opened"></wcs-notify>
<!-- state side: $commandTokens:["request","notify"], $eventTokens:["opened"],
     send() { this.$command.notify.emit("New message", { body:"...", tag:"chat", data:{room:7} }); },
     $on: { opened: (state, event) => { /* event.detail = {tag,data,action} */ } } -->
```
The reactive form binds the `notice` attribute (with same-value suppression; recommend debounce + `tag` to prevent spam).

**camera/recorder** — a raw MediaStream never enters state; wire elements directly to each other:
```html
<wcs-camera data-wcs="eventToken.streamReady: streamReady"></wcs-camera>
<wcs-recorder data-wcs="command.attachStream: $command.attachStream"></wcs-recorder>
<!-- $on: { streamReady: (state, ev) => state.$command.attachStream.emit(ev.detail) } -->
```
`streamReady` re-fires with a new stream on every re-acquire (switchCamera / constraint change / visibility resume) — this `$on` wiring re-attaches each time. Start the recorder only after a stream is attached (a stream-less `start` errors and warns `[wcs/command-not-ready]`). Bind `keepAlive: <recording path>` on the camera: hiding the tab otherwise suspends the stream and ends the take (4.5 warns `[wcs/camera-keep-alive-missing]`). Build the upload's file with the clip's type: `new File([blob], "clip.webm", { type: blob.type })`.

**defined** — a declarative readiness gate over tags whose load order you do not control (the correct replacement for `await customElements.whenDefined()` in a handler):
```html
<wcs-defined tags="wcs-tilt,wcs-accelerometer" timeout="5000"
  data-wcs="defined: sensorsReady; pending: sensorsPending; missing: sensorsMissing"></wcs-defined>
<button data-wcs="onclick: startGame; disabled: sensorsResolving; textContent: startLabel"></button>
<!-- state side: sensorsPending seeded with the tag list (so the control is held on first paint),
     get sensorsResolving() { return this.sensorsPending.length > 0; } -->
```
Gate on **`pending`**, not `defined`: `timeout` moves a never-arriving tag to `missing`, which releases the control into a degraded mode instead of locking the user out; a late arrival is still promoted out of `missing`, so a merely slow CDN self-heals. Outputs are monotonic and terminal, and all inputs are frozen at connect.

**midi** — one tag covers both directions (a page holds exactly one `MIDIAccess`). Take notes off the occurrence surface, not off a property:
```html
<wcs-midi auto channel="1" data-wcs="eventToken.message: onMidi; control: cc; value: ccValue"></wcs-midi>
<!-- $eventTokens: ["onMidi"],
     $on: { onMidi: (state, ev) => { const { type, note, velocity } = ev.detail; ... } } -->
```
Nothing starts on connect unless `auto` is set — `requestMIDIAccess()` can prompt — so otherwise fire `command.request` from a gesture. Two normalizations are already applied for you: **a note-on with velocity 0 is reported as `noteoff`** (many controllers never send a real note-off; the raw status byte stays in `message.data[0]` — decide from `type`, never from that byte, or keys stay stuck), and **velocity is 0-1** so it multiplies straight into a gain (do not divide by 127). Chromium-only and secure-context-only — elsewhere `permission` is `"unsupported"` rather than a throw, from the connect since 4.17 (`auto` or not). **In a route's content**: a disconnect publishes `connected: false` and (since 4.17) `devices: []`; put back, an element whose last `request()` got access requests again by itself while the permission is still granted (4.17; `auto` always did). Hide a Connect button on `connected`, not on `devices`. Device names are not unique; prefer ids when targeting a specific unit.

**audio** — structure in markup, numbers from state; commands carry the notes:
```html
<wcs-audio volume="0.7"
  data-wcs="command.noteOn: $command.play; command.noteOff: $command.stop; voices: activeVoices">
  <wcs-voice poly="8">
    <wcs-osc type="sawtooth" note detune="-7" out="vcf"></wcs-osc>
    <wcs-biquad id="vcf" type="lowpass" data-wcs="frequency: cutoff; q: resonance">
      <wcs-lfo type="sine" rate="4" param="frequency" data-wcs="depth: lfoDepth"></wcs-lfo>
      <wcs-env attack="0.01" decay="0.25" sustain="0.55" release="0.35" out="bus"></wcs-env>
    </wcs-biquad>
  </wcs-voice>
  <wcs-gain id="bus" gain="0.8"><wcs-delay time="0.28" feedback="0.35" mix="0.2"></wcs-delay></wcs-gain>
</wcs-audio>
<input type="range" min="80" max="8000" data-wcs="value: cutoff">
<!-- $commandTokens: ["play","stop"];  this.$command.play.emit(60, 0.9) -->
```
Bind only the numeric params (§1.1) — writing a structural attribute from state rebuilds the graph and cuts every sounding voice. To draw a scope, drive `<wcs-analyser>` from `<wcs-raf>` through the command/event tokens rather than owning a rAF loop:
```html
<wcs-raf data-wcs="eventToken.tick: onTick"></wcs-raf>
<wcs-analyser id="scope" master
  data-wcs="command.sample: $command.grab; eventToken.frame: onFrame"></wcs-analyser>
```

## 3. signals Quick Reference (`@wcstack/signals`)

### Positioning (when to use vs state)

- `@wcstack/state` connects UI and state through **HTML path strings** (`data-wcs`); no reactive primitives appear in code. `@wcstack/signals` conversely **exposes signal/computed/effect directly** (no DSL, no `data-wcs`). The two are not competitors — they **coexist**.
- Out of scope for signals v1: SSR/hydration, deep/proxy reactivity (path-based deep tracking is state's territory), stream backpressure.
- The API is a minimal in-house implementation modeled on the TC39 Signals proposal.

### CDN loading (one-entry-per-page rule)

```html
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": { "@wcstack/signals/dom": "https://esm.run/@wcstack/signals/dom" } }
</script>
<!-- pinned: the version goes before the sub-path — https://esm.run/@wcstack/signals@4.28.0/dom -->
<script type="module">
  import { signal, computed, effect, selector, delegateEvents, h, render, For, bindNode, mountNode } from "@wcstack/signals/dom";
</script>
```

> **Known trap**: on the CDN each entry is a self-contained bundle with the core embedded, so importing both `@wcstack/signals` and `@wcstack/signals/dom` on one page causes **reactive core duplication** and reactivity breaks at the seam. On CDN pages import everything from the single `/dom` entry (`/dom` re-exports the entire core). No such constraint with local npm / bundlers.

### Basic API (core)

```js
const count = signal(0);                       // .get()=read+track / .peek()=no tracking / .set(v)
const doubled = computed(() => count.get() * 2); // lazy, memoized, equality short-circuit
effect(() => { console.log(doubled.get()); });   // runs immediately once, then coalesced into a microtask
count.set(1);        // effect re-runs on the next microtask
flushSync();         // synchronous flush (when reading DOM back in tests)
createRoot((dispose) => { /* effects/resources inside are disposed all at once by dispose */ });
onCleanup(fn);       // register cleanup on the current owner
```

### DOM layer (`h` / `render` / `SignalsElement`)

`h(tag, props, ...children)` builds real DOM once; only function/signal props and children update via individual effects (no VDOM). A function under an `on…` key is an event listener: `onClick` → `click`, `onclick` / `"onadd-to-cart"` → the name as written (since 4.1 — a lowercase `onclick` used to run at render). **Pages behind `@wcstack/router`**: make each page a `SignalsElement` (renders on connect, disposes on disconnect — never `render()` into route content from outside: the router puts the same nodes back) and read params with `bindNode(document.querySelector("wcs-router")).signals.typedParams`. **A value kept in `<wcs-storage>`**: seed your signal from `store.signals.value.peek()` right after `mountNode`, *then* `bindInput` — the first `bindInput` run writes the signal into the element, so an empty seed saves over the stored value (the signals form of `#init=element`). For custom elements, extend `SignalsElement` and implement only `render()` (mounts on connect; disposes all effects on disconnect). An object or array prop for a custom element that is not defined yet is held and assigned through its setter once it is defined (4.2; it used to land as `"[object Object]"`) — primitives still go to the attribute. **Develop with `globalThis.__WCS_DEV__ = true`** set before the app's module: dev mode warns about unowned effects, unkeyed object rows and, since 4.2, a `computed` or effect whose first run read no signal (`UNTRACKED_COMPUTED` / `UNTRACKED_EFFECT` — it never runs again).

### Keyed lists — `For` / `Index`

```js
const todos = signal([{ id: 1, text: "a" }, { id: 2, text: "b" }]);
h("ul", null, For(todos, (t, index, current) => h("li", null, () => `${index()}: ${current().text}`), { key: (t) => t.id }));
// a keyed row is reused while its key is: `t` is the item the row was built with — read what changes through current() (4.1)
// for primitive arrays use Index: each is (item: () => T, index: number)
h("ul", null, Index(nums, (n) => h("li", null, () => String(n() * 2))));
```

A plain reactive child (`() => items.map(render)`) regenerates everything on every change, so always use For/Index for lists. Key default is `===`; duplicate keys throw. `each` returns a single Node.

**The selected row — `selector`** (4.18). `class: () => (selected.get() === row.id ? "active" : "")` re-runs every row on each change of the selection. `const isSelected = selector(selected)` — created under an owner (`createRoot` / a `SignalsElement` render) — gives `isSelected(key)`, and a change re-runs only the row it left and the row it took: `class: () => (isSelected(row.id) ? "active" : "")`. Keys compare as `Map` keys; to select an object, select its id: `selector(computed(() => selectedItem.get()?.id))`.

**Event delegation — `delegateEvents`** (4.19, opt-in). For a big list, call `delegateEvents(["click"])` once before building the view: `h()`'s `onClick` then waits on its element without a listener, and one listener on the document hands each click along its path (`currentTarget` and `this` are the element, `stopPropagation()` stops the outer handlers). Write the row's handler as usual — never one handler on the `<tbody>` that inspects `event.target`. Off by default because a delegated handler runs after the listeners of the elements in between, never for an element outside the document (a test that calls `el.click()` on an element it did not attach sees no call), and only for events that bubble and are composed (`click`, `input`, `keydown`, pointer / mouse, `focusin` / `focusout`); `focus`, `change`, `submit`, touch, wheel and custom events throw. Call it before the elements are made; pass the root for a closed shadow root.

### Async — `resource` / `streamResource`

```js
const user = resource(
  async (userId, signal) => (await fetch(`/api/users/${userId}`, { signal })).json(),
  { args: () => id.get() },  // when a signal read inside args changes → abort the previous run and restart (switchMap)
); // user.value / user.loading / user.error are read-only signals

const log = streamResource((args, signal) => openLogStream(signal), {
  fold: (acc, chunk) => [...(acc ?? []), chunk], initial: [],
}); // log.value / log.status ("idle"|"active"|"done"|"error") / log.error. No backpressure; keep fold bounded
```

Strong contract: `source` must always honor the `AbortSignal` it is passed (this is what drives restart/dispose).

### wc-bindable bridge — `bindNode` (turn I/O nodes into signals)

```js
const bound = bindNode(fetchEl);              // descriptor is auto-derived from constructor.wcBindable
bound.signals.value.get();                    // output property → read-only signal (same-value guard)
bound.on("fired", { fold, initial });         // event-token stream (fires every time, even on same value)
bound.set("url", v);                          // imperative write to an input
bound.bindInput("url", someSignal);           // reactive reflection of signal → input (loops are guarded)
bound.command("fetch", ...args);              // invoke a command
bound.bindCommand("start", trigger, mapArgs); // invoke command on trigger change (does not fire on the initial value)
bound.dispose();                              // tear down everything (idempotent; inert afterwards)
```

Typing via `bindNode<FetchShape>(el)`. Real-world pattern: `effect(() => bound.set("url", ...))` for the query → `<wcs-fetch>` auto-fetches → read `bound.signals.value` in a `computed` and render with `For` (examples/signals-live-search).

**What a property signal receives** (`bound.signals.x` and `bound.on("x")`): `getter(event)` from the descriptor, and when `getter` is omitted the wc-bindable default `(e) => e.detail` — the same rule as a `data-wcs` two-way binding, so an element behaves identically under `state` and `signals` (fixed in wcstack#238; earlier signals releases read the element property instead). The initial seed is the one property read (`el[name]`, there is no event yet). Every wcs-* node dispatches its value as `detail`, so nothing changes for them; a third-party element whose `detail` is not the property value (`detail: { value }`, or no `detail`) needs an explicit `getter: (e) => e.target.value` in the descriptor you pass to `bindNode`.

**`bindNode` is synchronous, so the class must already be registered when you call it** — it reads the descriptor from `el.constructor.wcBindable`, and an un-upgraded element has none (it throws — since 4.2 saying the tag is not defined yet). This is the structural asymmetry with `data-wcs`: the declarative layer can defer wiring until upgrade, an imperative API that returns values now cannot. Pick the idiom by who loads the node (`docs/signals-definition-timing.md`):

| Situation | Idiom | Failure behavior |
|---|---|---|
| App loads a **required** node | side-effect `import "@wcstack/<pkg>/auto"` + `mountNode(tag)` | module-graph evaluation failure — loud, correct for a node the app cannot run without |
| App loads an **optional** node | `import("@wcstack/<pkg>/auto").then(() => mountNode(tag)).catch(degrade)` | `import()` **rejects** on load failure — a real per-package failure boundary |
| A tag **you do not load** (autoloader, mixed state+signals page, third-party script) | `await customElements.whenDefined(tag)` then `bindNode(el)`, or a `<wcs-defined>` gate | `whenDefined` **never rejects** — pending forever; use `<wcs-defined timeout>` when the UX needs a failure signal |
| Pure-logic node, **JS only** (no element, no `:state()`, no state coexistence) | `bindNode(new XxxCore())` | plain import semantics — **the registry is not involved, so definition timing does not exist** |

`whenDefined` is the last resort for tags you do not own, not the default recipe — no `whenDefined` call remains in any repo demo. **Split static vs dynamic import by what is lost when that import fails**, not by convenience: the first pass at converting `signals-tilt-maze` put `wakelock` on the static import, and one decorative package's CDN failure blanked the entire page again — exactly the failure mode the conversion was meant to remove. Only a node the app cannot exist without belongs on a static import; everything else takes the `import().then(mountNode).catch(degrade)` form (with a `Promise.race` timeout if the UX needs a deadline).

### `mountNode` — create + bind + mount a headless node (`@wcstack/signals/dom`)

```js
import "@wcstack/fetch/auto";                 // defines <wcs-fetch>; the module graph guarantees the order
import { mountNode } from "@wcstack/signals/dom";

const fetcher = mountNode("wcs-fetch", { attrs: { url: "/api/people" } });
fetcher.signals.value.get();                  // the full BoundNode surface
fetcher.el;                                   // the created element (connected)
fetcher.unmount();                            // dispose() + remove the element (idempotent)
```

On a buildless page the side-effect import is what carries the ordering guarantee, so it has to be a real `import` inside the module — add `"@wcstack/fetch/auto": "https://esm.run/@wcstack/fetch/auto"` to the import map (or import the full URL directly). A `<script src=".../auto">` tag in `<head>` also works because module scripts execute in document order, but then the guarantee lives in the HTML rather than in the module graph.

Signature: `mountNode(tagName, { attrs?, parent?, descriptor? })` → `BoundNode & { el, unmount() }`. The internal order **is** the contract: create → set `attrs` → `bindNode` → connect. Attributes land before `connectedCallback` (shells read their config there) and the adapter subscribes before connect, so an event fired from `connectedCallback` cannot be missed. `attrs` follow HTML boolean semantics (`true` → empty attribute, `false` → omitted, everything else stringified); `parent` defaults to `document.body`; the tag name is lower-cased for you. An undefined tag throws a descriptive error immediately instead of hanging. Like `bindNode` it is not tied to a reactive owner — tear down explicitly, or compose `onCleanup(() => m.unmount())`. On a `MountedNode`, **`dispose()` is an alias of `unmount()`** (it owns the element's lifecycle, so the familiar verb never leaves a connected element with live I/O behind).

### Binding a Core directly — no element at all (normative)

Every I/O node splits into a framework-agnostic **Core** and a custom-element **Shell**, and the Core alone is a complete wc-bindable node: it extends `EventTarget`, dispatches on itself by default (`constructor(target?)`, `target ?? this`), exposes observables as public getters, and carries `static wcBindable` — so `bindNode` resolves the descriptor with no second argument:

```js
import { FetchCore } from "@wcstack/fetch";
import { bindNode } from "@wcstack/signals/dom";

const core = new FetchCore();
const bound = bindNode(core);   // descriptor from FetchCore.wcBindable — no element involved
core.fetch("/api/user");        // commands are plain methods
bound.signals.value.get();
```

This surface is normative across every wcstack I/O node (`docs/async-io-node-guidelines.md` §3.9 — audited at 38 Cores, zero deviations; the audit predates v1.25's `AudioGraphCore` / `MidiCore`, both of which ship the same shape) and semver-protected: entry export, `EventTarget` inheritance, self-dispatch default, `static wcBindable`, getter-readable observables, `observe()`/`dispose()`/`ready`, never-throw, and headless construction (`target` always optional). Constructor **config** arguments stay per-package — check that package's README. Trade-off: you drive the lifecycle yourself (`observe()`/`dispose()` or the start/stop commands, e.g. `onCleanup(() => core.dispose())`), and you give up attribute config plus `:state()` CSS reflection (a Shell/ElementInternals feature). Fits pure-logic nodes (fetch / websocket / sse / broadcast / timer / debounce / defined / raf …); element-coupled nodes (intersection & resize targets, camera preview, fullscreen / pip / pointer-lock) keep earning their Shell.

### Stability

The core (signal/computed/effect/createRoot/onCleanup/flushSync) and resource/streamResource are **Stable**. `bindNode`/`nodeSource` and the DOM layer (h/For/Index/SignalsElement/`mountNode`) are **Evolving** (may change in minor releases).


---

# Reference: a page wcstack does not own (islands and widgets)

<!-- source: wcstack-skill/skills/wcstack-app/references/islands.md -->

# wcstack on a page it does not own — islands and widgets

Sources: `docs/islands.md` (+ `.ja.md`), `packages/state/README.md` "Inserting markup yourself" and "Mounting Additional State", `docs/binder-protocol-design.md` §10, `docs/scoped-custom-element-registries.md`, `packages/state/src/features/release.ts`, `packages/state/src/features/diagnostics.ts`, and the `community-hall` seam app in `docs/seam-apps.md` (a CMS site with htmx 2, five islands, a widget on a Turbo site that runs wcstack 4.17). All verified against the actual files at v4.28.0; the htmx and Turbo frame snippets below were run in Chromium.

Read this before adding wcstack to a server-rendered site whose pages come from another template language and are swapped by htmx or Turbo, or before writing a widget that other sites paste into their pages. Everything else in this skill still applies inside the island.

## 1. Where the root goes

- **One root `<wcs-state>` per page, inside the body the navigator swaps** (htmx's `hx-boost`, Turbo Drive). The old root leaves with the old body; the new page's root binds the new page. Every island of the page is a key of that one state (`booking.*`, `filter.*`) — separate roots on one document collide (`[wcs/second-root]`, `#47`, the winner depends on load timing).
- **Never keep the root across a swap** (`hx-preserve`): the old root stays bound to the old page and the new page's markup is never walked.
