- **What the server knows about the page** reaches the state as data: a `<script type="application/json" id="page-seed">` read in `$connectedCallback`, or a volume with `json=`.
- **A state module loaded with `src=`** is fine on every page since 4.20: each `<wcs-state>` naming it gets its own evaluation. On a page pinned to 4.19 or earlier, they shared one object — build the state inline from a factory instead.
- **The server's template language uses `{{ }}` too:** declare `$behavior: { enableMustache: false }` and write bindings as `data-wcs` and comment bindings (`<!--@@: total|locale-->`). Never put wcstack's `{{ }}` inside such a template — the server renders it first. The lint follows the declaration since 4.20.

## 2. Markup another library inserts

The state walks its root once. Markup inserted later — an htmx swap into `#results`, a Turbo frame, an `innerHTML` — keeps its `data-wcs` and does nothing until it is handed to the binder (since 4.20 the diagnostics warn `[wcs/inserted-unbound]` a second later).

```js
const binder = () => globalThis[Symbol.for("wcstack.binder")];
const REGIONS = "#results, #booking";   // the regions the page's htmx swaps into

// htmx: htmx:load for each element a swap inserted; htmx:beforeCleanupElement for each it removes
document.addEventListener("htmx:load", (e) => {
  if (e.detail.elt.parentElement?.closest(REGIONS)) binder()?.bind(e.detail.elt);
});
document.addEventListener("htmx:beforeCleanupElement", (e) => {
  // a region's own children — what the server rendered there first too, which the page walk bound
  if (e.detail.elt.parentElement?.matches(REGIONS)) binder()?.release?.(e.detail.elt);
});

// Turbo frames: the frame element stays and its children are replaced
document.addEventListener("turbo:before-frame-render", (e) => {
  for (const el of e.target.children) binder()?.release?.(el);
});
document.addEventListener("turbo:frame-render", (e) => {
  for (const el of e.target.children) binder()?.bind(el);
});
```

- **Hand over the new nodes, never their container.** An element the walk visited is left alone, with everything in it: `bind(#results)` after a swap into `#results` binds nothing.
- **A `for:` / `if:` template at the top of a fragment** is not rendered when handed over (`#204`): put it inside an element.
- **`release(subtree)`** (4.20, binder protocol version 2, the `release` add-on — in `/auto` and `.`; a `/core` page installs `@wcstack/state/features/release`) lets go of a subtree thrown away for good — whatever is bound under it, handed over or bound by the page walk (the server's first results). Without it, every set of results ever shown stays bound and every change writes into all of them. Released nodes are not bound again — hand over new markup. Never release content that comes back.
- **The binder is `undefined` until `@wcstack/state` has loaded**; markup inserted before that is bound by the first walk.
- **htmx attributes inside a `for:` / `if:` template** do nothing (rows are cloned after htmx processed the page), and a bound `attr.hx-get:` is not seen either. Keep `hx-*` outside wcstack templates.
- **htmx acts during the event's dispatch; bindings apply a microtask later.** Decide in htmx's own events (`htmx:confirm`), not on an attribute a binding sets.
- **One owner per element:** never let the server replace an element a binding renders (`hx-swap-oob`) — the new element is not bound.

## 3. History caches

htmx's history snapshot and Turbo's snapshot cache restore a page **as drawn**: no `<template>` left, comment bindings turned to text — it looks right and never updates (since 4.20 the diagnostics warn `[wcs/rendered-copy]`). On pages with islands, turn the cache off so that Back loads the page from the server:

```html
<body hx-boost="true" hx-history="false">
<!-- Turbo -->
<meta name="turbo-cache-control" content="no-cache">
```

## 4. A widget on another site's page

A page defines `<wcs-state>` once: the first copy of `@wcstack/state` it evaluates defines it, a second copy does nothing (`[wcs/package-twice]`). A widget that loads `/auto` on a page that runs wcstack therefore runs on the page's copy, of whatever version. Give the widget a shadow root with a scoped registry and define wcstack's tags into it — every package's `bootstrapXxx(config, registry)` takes the registry:

```js
import { bootstrapState } from "https://esm.run/@wcstack/state@4.28.0";
import { bootstrapSse } from "https://esm.run/@wcstack/sse@4.28.0";

let registry = null;
function widgetRegistry() {
  if (registry === null) {
    registry = new CustomElementRegistry();
    bootstrapSse(undefined, registry);
    bootstrapState(undefined, registry);
  }
  return registry;
}

class PartnerWidget extends HTMLElement {
  connectedCallback() {
    if (this.shadowRoot) return;
    const shadow = this.attachShadow({ mode: "open", customElementRegistry: widgetRegistry() });
    shadow.innerHTML = `<wcs-state src="${new URL("./widget-state.js", import.meta.url)}"></wcs-state>…`;
  }
}
customElements.define("partner-widget", PartnerWidget);
```

- Import the main entries (they export `bootstrapXxx`), never `/auto` (it defines into the page's global registry), and pin the version.
- The shadow root is the widget's own root: one state tree beside the page's, and neither stylesheet reaches the other.
- Scoped registries ship in Chrome / Edge 146 and Safari 26; **Firefox has not shipped them** — where `new CustomElementRegistry()` throws, show a fallback (a link to the full page) rather than run on the page's copy.
- Turbo's snapshot is a clone, and a clone has no shadow root: the widget starts again in `connectedCallback`. Under `data-turbo-preview` on `<html>` show a placeholder.

## 5. Checking

- The lint reads templates in which `{{ }}` is the server's syntax, and fragments without a `<wcs-state>` (`wcs/state-absent` since 4.20 — their paths are not checked). To check a fragment's paths, lint the pages as rendered: render through the server, put each fragment into its page, run `npx @wcstack/lint --root=<public dir>` on the result.
- A main-flow e2e test that fails on any console warning catches `[wcs/inserted-unbound]` and `[wcs/rendered-copy]`.
- `@wcstack/testing` imports a state module anew for each `mount()`, so page-to-page flows (a second page, a second instance) belong in a browser test.


---

# Reference: forms (a page that is mostly a form)

<!-- source: wcstack-skill/skills/wcstack-app/references/forms.md -->

# Forms — a page that is mostly a form

Sources: `docs/forms.md` (+ `.ja.md`), `packages/state/README.md` "Forms: what happens outside the `input` event" and "Two-Way Binding", `packages/state/src/features/forms.ts`, `docs/timing-and-firing-contract.md` §25, `packages/fetch/README.md`, `docs/seam-apps.md` (ekiden-entry). Verified against wcstack 4.28.0; every snippet here was run in Chromium.

Read this before building an application form, an entry sheet or a wizard: text typed with an IME (Japanese, Chinese, Korean), fields that format what is typed, autofill, a reset button, rows of inputs that move, form controls of your own.

## 1. What `@wcstack/state` does (4.23, the `forms` add-on)

In `/auto`, `.` and the `wcstack/auto` bundle; a split page installs `@wcstack/state/features/forms`. On a page pinned to 4.22 or earlier none of this happens, and each case below goes wrong without a word.

- **A field being composed is not written.** While an IME composition is on, the bindings that write the field's `value` wait, and are applied when it is over with the value state has then. So a setter may normalize what is typed, and a write from elsewhere (another tab's draft, a looked-up address) does not break the composition.
- **A value with no `input` event reaches state**: on `change` (an autofill that fires `change` alone), and for each field of a form before its `submit` handlers run (a value put in silently).
- **After a reset** (`<button type="reset">`, `form.reset()`) each bound control writes its reset value to state and is written from state again.
- **Before state binds the form** (the router drew it while the root state loads), nothing is lost and nothing is sent:
  - the browser never sends a form whose submit is prevented (`onsubmit#prevent`);
  - a submit made then is made again once the form is bound, with the button pressed;
  - what the user typed is given back and told to state.

  Disable the submit button while sending (`disabled: sending`), or a click before binding and another after it send twice. Not covered: a form in a shadow root, and a server-rendered form before any script runs — give that one a `method` and an `action` of its own.
- These are told to state by an `input` (and `change`) event that does not bubble, dispatched on the control: a delegated `oninput:` handler does not run for them.

## 2. Text composed with an IME

- A two-way binding writes every composition step to state. Code that must see finished text only: `if (e.isComposing) return;` in the `oninput:` handler, and `oncompositionend:` for the final text.
- **Enter confirms a conversion and reaches your `keydown` handler.** Always:

```js
onKey(e) {
  // 229: Safari sends the confirming Enter after compositionend, with isComposing already false
  if (e.key !== "Enter" || e.isComposing || e.keyCode === 229) return;
  this.next();
}
```

- **A reading (フリガナ) field** takes the kana from `compositionupdate` — once converted, the field's value is the kanji and the reading is gone:

```html
<input data-wcs="value: name; oncompositionupdate: reading; oncompositionend: readingEnd">
<input data-wcs="value: kana">
```

```js
name: "", kana: "", _reading: "",
reading(e) { if (/^[ぁ-ゖァ-ヺー]+$/.test(e.data)) this._reading = e.data; },
readingEnd() {
  this.kana += this._reading.replace(/[ぁ-ゖ]/g, (c) => String.fromCharCode(c.charCodeAt(0) + 0x60));
  this._reading = "";
},
```

- Tests: a real composition can be driven in Chromium only (CDP `Input.imeSetComposition` / `Input.insertText`). happy-dom has no IME — dispatch `compositionstart` / `compositionend` yourself.

## 3. A field that changes what is typed

- **Normalize in a setter** — `get phone()` formats, `set phone(v)` keeps the digits. Not on every keystroke in a handler that rewrites the field.
- **Never an output filter on a two-way field** (`value: price|locale`, `value: code|upper`): the field is rewritten on every keystroke, and state receives the formatted text. Lint `wcs/two-way-output-filter`. Show the formatted value in another element.
- **The caret goes to the end** when a write changes the field's text. For a field edited in the middle, write back on commit: `value#onchange: phone`. To format while typing and keep the caret, bind one way and write the field yourself:

```html
<input data-wcs="value#ro: phone; oninput: typePhone">
```

```js
typePhone(e) {
  if (e.isComposing) return;
  const el = e.target;
  const digitsBefore = el.value.slice(0, el.selectionStart).replace(/\D/g, "").length;
  this.phoneDigits = el.value.replace(/\D/g, "");
  const text = this.phone;
  el.value = text;
  let i = 0;
  for (let seen = 0; i < text.length && seen < digitsBefore; i++) if (/\d/.test(text[i])) seen++;
  el.setSelectionRange(i, i);
}
```

- **An input filter converts on the way in only** (`value|trim: name`): state gets the trimmed text, the field stays as typed.
- **Numbers**: an element's `value` is a string — `count + 1` is `"51"`. `valueAsNumber: count` (number, range, date and time types) or `value|number: count` (`|int`, `|float`). Lint `wcs/number-written-as-string`. An emptied `valueAsNumber:` field gives `NaN`; `value|number:` gives `0`.

## 4. Values the user did not type

- Give each field a `name` and an `autocomplete` token, inside a `<form>`.
- **Send from the form's `submit` handler**, with the step's button as the submit button: a value put in with no event is told to state right before that handler, not before.
- **Send what state holds**, never `new FormData(form)`: the page holds only the step that is rendered.
- A reset takes the markup's defaults. A radio group with no `checked` radio in the markup has no reset value: state keeps its value and the radio shows it again. When the defaults live in state, write a `clear()` method and a plain button.

## 5. Rows of inputs

- **Reorder the objects** (`this.rows = [b, a, ...rest]`, the same objects): focus, an open `<details>`, a chosen file and a composition travel with the row (Chromium 133+, Firefox 144+; Safari re-inserts the row and the field loses the focus — `element.focus()` after).
- **Never exchange the values between rows**: what the elements hold stays at the position.
- **A list rebuilt from JSON needs `$listKeys`**, or every row is re-created.
- **A row's radios need a name per row**: `attr.name: .sexGroup` with `get "runners.*.sexGroup"() { return "sex-" + this[".id"]; }`. A literal `name` makes one group of all the rows (lint `wcs/radio-name-shared`).
- **Keep a server's errors by the row's id** (`errorsById[runner.id]`), not by index.
- **`<wcs-upload>` / `<wcs-fetch>` in a row that moves**: since 4.23 the request goes on where the browser moves the row with `moveBefore()` (Chromium, Firefox). In Safari the row is taken out and put back and the request is aborted: do not reorder while a row's request is in flight, or keep the I/O elements in a list that does not move.

## 6. Steps (a wizard)

- **Render a step with `if:` or a route; never hide it.** A hidden step's `required` fields make the browser refuse the submit, with nothing shown. Validate the whole entry in state before the last send.
- **Focus a field of the next step after it is rendered**: emit the focus command from `$renderedCallback`, or when the router's `path` changes. Emitted with the step change it is lost (`[wcs/command-token-unbound]`).
- **A `422` naming a field of another step**: keep errors in state by field, go to the first step that has one, focus once it is rendered.
- **A guard that shares code with the page** imports a full URL inside the function — `await import(new URL("/js/guards.js", location.href).href)` — or an import-map name: a guard is a `blob:` module, and `"./guards.js"` does not resolve.

## 7. Form controls of your own

A form-associated custom element (`static formAssociated = true`) binds like any wc-bindable element — with `value` in **both** lists:

```js
class MidoriStepper extends HTMLElement {
  static formAssociated = true;
  static wcBindable = {
    protocol: "wc-bindable", version: 1,
    properties: [{ name: "value", event: "midori-stepper:change" }],
    inputs: [{ name: "value" }],
  };
  #internals = this.attachInternals();
  #value = 0;
  get value() { return this.#value; }
  set value(v) { this.#set(Number(v) || 0); }               // from state or script: no event
  #set(v) { this.#value = v; this.#internals.setFormValue(String(v)); this.#render(); }
  #changed(v) {                                              // from the user: tell
    this.#set(v);
    this.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent("midori-stepper:change", { detail: v, bubbles: true }));
  }
  formResetCallback() { this.#changed(0); }
  formStateRestoreCallback(state) { this.#changed(Number(state) || 0); }
  #render() { /* draw the value */ }
}
```

- `value` in `properties` only: state never writes the control, and its first value replaces state's — a saved draft is lost as the page loads. In `inputs` only, or with no declaration: what the user enters never reaches state. Since 4.23 the diagnostics warn (`[wcs/form-control-one-way]`); the lint does not read a class in another file.
- Dispatch the event on the user's change, on a reset and on a restore. A setter for every input: state writes properties, not attributes.

## 8. Sending

```html
<form data-wcs="onsubmit: send">…</form>
<wcs-fetch url="/api/entries" method="POST" manual data-wcs="body: payload; trigger: sending; error: sendError"></wcs-fetch>
```

```js
send(e) {
  e.preventDefault();
  this.payload = { ...this.entry };      // a new object each time
  this.sending = true;                   // after body: bindings apply in the order written
}
```

- **`body` before `trigger`**, in the `data-wcs` and in the method. A `command.fetch:` runs at once, before the bindings of the same update: its request carries the body the element had before.
- **A body is sent once.** Writing the same string again is no change, so a retry goes out with no body — write a new object each time. Since 4.23 `<wcs-fetch>` warns (`[wcs/fetch-body-gone]`).


---

# Reference: long lists (infinite scroll, rows, a window of rows, coming back)

<!-- source: wcstack-skill/skills/wcstack-app/references/long-lists.md -->

# Long lists

A page with a long list: infinite scroll, a feed, a table of thousands of rows, a list the user comes back to. Sources: `docs/long-lists.md` (+ `.ja.md`), `packages/fetch/README.md` §5, `packages/intersection/README.md`, `docs/timing-and-firing-contract.md` §26, the router README "Where route content lives", `docs/seam-apps.md` (town-archive). Verified against wcstack 4.28.0; the infinite-scroll example, the abort on a filter change and the link back to a row's fragment were run in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit. What says 4.24 needs that release; on 4.23 see the notes.

## 1. What costs

`@wcstack/state` does not slow down with the list: one row written at 3,000 rows is about a millisecond, and a getter that walks 12,000 rows through `this.items` is under 0.1 ms. The browser's work on the document grows: a page of 60 cards (about ten elements each) shows in about 20 ms at 120 cards and 30 to 95 ms at 3,000, depending on the browser — and about half as much again with two `<wcs-intersect>` around every card. A few hundred rows in the document are fine; at thousands, render a window (§4).

## 2. Loading a page at a time

```html
<style>wcs-infinite-scroll { display: block; min-height: 1px; }</style>
<wcs-fetch id="page-fetch" manual
  data-wcs="url: nextUrl; loading: listLoading; error: listError; eventToken.value: pageArrived; command.abort: $command.cancelPage"></wcs-fetch>
<ul><template data-wcs="for: items"><li data-wcs="textContent: .name"></li></template></ul>
<wcs-infinite-scroll target="page-fetch" root-margin="240px 0px" data-wcs="disabled: noMore"></wcs-infinite-scroll>
```

```js
export default {
  pageSize: 20, page: 1, items: [], noMore: false, listLoading: false, listError: null, filter: "",
  $eventTokens: ["pageArrived"],
  $commandTokens: ["cancelPage"],
  get nextUrl() { return "/api/items?page=" + this.page + "&limit=" + this.pageSize + "&q=" + encodeURIComponent(this.filter); },
  setFilter(event) {
    this.$command.cancelPage.emit(); // the page on its way is another list's: a manual fetch does not abort on a new url
    this.filter = event.target.value;
    this.items = [];
    this.page = 1;
    this.noMore = false;
  },
  $on: {
    pageArrived(state, event) {
      const { status, value } = event.detail;
      if (status < 200 || status >= 300) return; // a failure: the page number stays
      state.items = state.items.concat(value);
      state.page = state.page + 1;
      if (value.length < state.pageSize) state.noMore = true;
    },
  },
};
```

- The `url` comes from state, never a static attribute for page 1 (the first answer can arrive before state has bound the element).
- 4.24: the sentinel loads the first page when state writes the url, goes on while a page leaves it on screen, never repeats a failed request (the user scrolls away and back, or a retry button writes `trigger`), and stops at a response that added no row. (4.24.0 asked for one page ahead when the user was scrolling as a page landed; 4.24.1 does not.) **On 4.23 it does none of these** — use `<wcs-intersect target="self">` with `eventToken.intersecting:`, a first page asked from `$connectedCallback`, and `command.reobserve:` after each page that lands (never after a failure), as `examples/state-intersect-fetch` does.
- Put the sentinel right after the list, **above** a spinner or a message shown while a page loads, so that only rows move it. A spinner inserted above it when a request starts pushes it out of its margin, a scroll that goes on brings it back, and a request that failed in between is asked again.
- `<wcs-intersect>` is still the element for an edge the page schedules itself (a list that grows at both ends): act on the report, not on a stored flag; ask for the page the list's length says, not `page++`.
- `root` is the element that scrolls (an id or a selector, 4.24); a root that does not scroll counts everything in it as on screen. `root-margin` lengths need `px` or `%`.

## 3. Rows

- Keep the row objects: `items.concat(page)`. A list rebuilt as copies rebuilds every row in the document (focus lost, images decoded again).
- Write one row: `this.$update("items.*.fav", [index], (v) => !v)`.
- A flag per row, not a search per row: keep `fav` on the row (set when the page arrives, from a `Set`) instead of `this.favorites.some(…)` in a row getter. `$eq` is for one selected value; it has no set form.
- Images: native `loading="lazy"`, and the card in the photo's shape (`aspect-ratio`) so nothing moves.
- A per-row `<wcs-intersect>` only for what needs it ("seen"); `threshold="1"` never reports a card taller than the root — use `0.5`.
- A ★ on a card that is a link: the button beside the link, in one wrapper. Handlers are delegated: use the index the handler receives, not `event.currentTarget`.

## 4. A window of rows

For thousands of rows on screen. Row heights known without the document (fixed, or computed from the data); `for:` over a getter that slices the list, in a box as tall as the whole list; the scroll position from one passive `scroll` listener added in `$connectedCallback`, read once a frame and written to state (no wcstack element reports it); the container's width from `<wcs-resize target="self" round>` (a hidden container reports `0`: keep the last real width in a setter). Decide who anchors the scroll: `overflow-anchor: none` on the list when it places its own rows. With `@wcstack/signals`: `For` with a `key`, `current()`, `selector()`, `delegateEvents()` before the table is built. Not worth it below a few hundred rows.

## 5. Coming back

Back restores the position by itself when the list still holds its rows. A link of your own back to a row: navigate to its fragment — `this.navigateUrl = "/#photo-" + id` — not `scrollIntoView()` from a `$watch` (`references/router-and-scaffold.md`). A reload is the page's: keep the filter and the first row on screen in `<wcs-storage type="session">`.


---

# Reference: screen and sensor APIs (a tap, is it there, the iPhone, fullscreen, pickers)

<!-- source: wcstack-skill/skills/wcstack-app/references/device-apis.md -->

# Screen and sensor APIs

A page that uses what the device has: fullscreen, a small video window (Picture-in-Picture), the pointer lock, the screen's orientation, which way the phone points and how it moves, the share sheet, the contact picker, saved passwords, the eye dropper. Sources: `docs/device-apis.md` (+ `.ja.md`), the READMEs of `fullscreen`, `picture-in-picture`, `pointer-lock`, `screen-orientation`, `tilt`, `accelerometer`, `gyroscope`, `magnetometer`, `ambient-light-sensor`, `share`, `contacts`, `credential`, `eyedropper`, `permission`, `docs/timing-and-firing-contract.md` §8, §9, §16, §27. Written from the `stamp-rally` seam app. Verified against wcstack 4.28.0: the examples were run in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit; what is said about a phone was checked with stand-ins, not on a phone.

Three things hold for all of them: every one is missing on some device, every one that acts wants a tap, and none of them throws — a refusal is a value in `error` / `errorInfo`.

## 1. A tap

Fullscreen, Picture-in-Picture, the pointer lock, the share sheet, the pickers and the iPhone's sensor question are given only while the page handles a tap, a click or a key press. Chromium keeps a tap's activation about five seconds — so a page that emits late works on a fast network and fails on a slow one.

- Emit in the tap's handler, before anything is awaited. `onclick: $command.x` and a state method that emits synchronously are both inside the event.
- Do not emit from a `$watch`, when a response arrives, or after an `await`. Prepare what the command needs beforehand (make the picture when the card is shown, not in the tap) and disable the button until it is ready.
- A command for an element the same update renders has nothing to act on yet (a `<wcs-fullscreen>` whose `target` is in an `if:` the handler just opened): emit after the render.
- **A command that takes data is emitted from a state method.** `onclick: $command.share` passes the event as the data: `share(event)`, `select(event)`, `lock(event)` end in the browser's `TypeError`, `<wcs-credential>`'s `get(event)` resolves `null` without a word (lint `wcs/command-event-argument`, 4.25). Commands with no data — `requestFullscreen`, `start`, `open` — and `<wcs-fetch>`'s `fetch`, `<wcs-ws>`'s `close`, `<wcs-idle>`'s `start` (4.25) can be wired straight.

```js
$commandTokens: ["share"],
shareCard() {                               // in the tap
  this.$command.share.emit({ files: [this.cardFile], text: "…" });
},
```

## 2. Failures

Bind `errorInfo` on every element whose command the user triggers, and show something for it. `errorInfo.code`: `capability-missing` (the API is not there — offer the fallback), `not-allowed` (refused: no tap, a policy, a permission), `invalid-argument` (a `target` that names nothing), and the element's own code. `cancelled` is separate: the user closing the share sheet, the eye dropper or the contact picker is not a failure — show nothing.

```html
<wcs-share data-wcs="command.share: $command.share; cancelled: shareCancelled; errorInfo: shareError"></wcs-share>
<p role="alert" data-wcs="hidden: shareError|not">共有できませんでした。</p>
```

Since 4.25 the `diagnostics` add-on (in `/auto`) warns `[wcs/io-error-unobserved]` when an element reports a failure and its `data-wcs` reads none of `error`, `errorInfo`, `status`, `connected` and has no event token. Up to 4.24 such a failure was silent.

## 3. Is it there?

Since 4.25 each of the thirteen elements has a `supported` output: this page can use the feature — the API is there and no `Permissions-Policy` or `<iframe>` forbids it. Offer the button only when it is true (`hidden: fsSupported|not`). It is read when the binding attaches, so the first paint is right. On a page pinned to 4.24 or earlier there is no `supported`: detect by hand (`document.fullscreenEnabled`, `typeof EyeDropper`).

Where it is `false`: fullscreen on an iPhone (no element fullscreen), Picture-in-Picture in Firefox, the share sheet on most desktops, the eye dropper and saved passwords outside Chromium, the contact picker outside Android and in any frame, the Generic Sensor classes with no `devicemotion` beside them.

It does **not** say the user will allow it, that an orientation lock will hold (known only by trying, in fullscreen), or that the device has a sensor (a desktop has the events and never a reading: treat "no reading a moment after `start`" as "not here").

`<wcs-permission>` says `unsupported` for both "the browser cannot say" and "the page is forbidden"; since 4.25 `unsupportedReason` tells them apart: `policy-blocked` (tell the user to open the page itself in a new tab), `insecure-context`, `no-permissions-api`, `unknown-name` (Firefox and Safari reject the sensor names — it does not mean the feature is absent).

## 4. The iPhone's sensors

Safari on iOS gives no orientation or motion reading until the user allowed it, asks only from a tap, and asks separately for orientation (`<wcs-tilt>`) and motion (`<wcs-accelerometer>` / `<wcs-gyroscope>`, which read `devicemotion` there since 4.25). One token asks every question and one starts every sensor:

```html
<wcs-tilt data-wcs="permissionState: tiltPermission; heading: heading; errorInfo: tiltError;
                    command.requestPermission: $command.ask; command.start: $command.start"></wcs-tilt>
<wcs-accelerometer data-wcs="errorInfo: motionError; eventToken.x: moved;
                    command.requestPermission: $command.ask; command.start: $command.start"></wcs-accelerometer>
<button data-wcs="onclick: allow">許可する</button>
```

```js
$commandTokens: ["ask", "start"],
$eventTokens: ["moved"],
allow() { this.$command.ask.emit(); this.$command.start.emit(); },   // both in the tap, nothing awaited
```

- Never start the sensors at page load with nothing for the question: on an iPhone no reading ever arrives, and nothing says why.
- A question asked outside a tap is refused without being shown: `errorInfo.code` `not-allowed`, `recoverable: true`, and since 4.25 `permissionState` stays as it was (up to 4.24 it said `"denied"` — do not tell the user they refused). `"denied"` is the user's answer; Safari then does not ask again.
- After a reload `permissionState` is `"unknown"` again; a page that wants to remember keeps its own note.
- **North** is `<wcs-tilt>`'s `heading` (4.25; degrees clockwise from north, `null` until known). `alpha` is relative on both phone platforms — never turn a compass by it. Show the direction as text while `heading` is `null`.
- On a page pinned to 4.24 or earlier: `<wcs-accelerometer>` / `<wcs-gyroscope>` are `capability-missing` on an iPhone and there is no `heading` — a hand-written `devicemotion` / `deviceorientationabsolute` listener is needed there.

## 5. Fullscreen, the lock, the small window

- Bind `active`. Do not keep "is it fullscreen" as a flag the buttons flip: the user leaves with Escape, a swipe or the window's ×, and the flag does not know.
- Never assign the bound path (`this.isFullscreen = true` fills no screen — lint `wcs/output-path-written`): ask the element with its command.
- `target` is a CSS selector: `target="#viewer"`, not `target="viewer"` (lint `wcs/target-selector`).
- Hold the screen in landscape from a `$watch` on the path bound to `active` — `true` → emit `lock` with `"landscape"`, `false` → emit `unlock` — never in the handler that requests fullscreen (it is not active yet).
- **What must go on across pages lives outside the router.** A route's content is taken out of the document on leaving: the browser ends fullscreen and the pointer lock, and a video in Picture-in-Picture belongs outside the routes with its `<wcs-pip>`, hidden with a class where it is not shown (Chromium keeps a removed video playing, so the mistake does not show there). Since 4.25 the element reports `active: false` as it leaves; up to 4.24 state kept `true`.

## 6. Sensors that keep running

No sensor element starts on connect, a disconnect stops it, and nothing starts it again when its route comes back: emit `start` when the page that needs it is shown and `stop` when it is not (a `$watch` on the route), and stop on a hidden tab (no element reports visibility — `docs/long-lived-pages.md`). Do not bind every reading into state and draw a list from it: take the readings in an event-token handler (`event.detail` is the whole reading, `{ x, y, z }`) and write a path only when what is shown changes. `frequency` is a positive number of Hz (`"60hz"` means the default rate; lint `wcs/frequency-invalid`).

## 7. Pickers and saved passwords

- **contacts**: every member of a result is an array (`name: ["山田 花子"]`, possibly empty). Give `value` a slot of its own and make your own records from it in a `$watch` — never bind it into a list the page keeps (`value` is an output: at bind the element's `null` replaces what the path had). A picker closed without a choice is `cancelled` (4.25; up to 4.24 it wrote `value: []`).
- **credential**: store the pair only after the server accepted it (`store({ id, password })`, 4.25; before, build `new PasswordCredential(…)` behind a `typeof` check). On sign-out emit `preventSilentAccess` (4.25; before, call `navigator.credentials.preventSilentAccess()` by hand) or the next visit signs the user back in. Keep the plain form in a shape a password manager fills.
- **share**: ask `canShare({ files })` (a method of the element) before handing over a file; fall back to the text and the link, then to copying the link.

## 8. Testing

Stand-ins: Chromium's DevTools protocol for sensor readings (`Emulation.setSensorOverrideEnabled` / `setSensorOverrideReadings`); `page.addInitScript` scripts for the iPhone's question, the share sheet and the pickers, which answer only with `navigator.userActivation.isActive`. A call that is "not a tap" must come from the page's own timer on a page the test has not touched: Playwright's clicks, `page.evaluate()` and the polling behind `expect(locator)` all count as user activation. Headless Chromium's `screen.orientation.lock()` resolves and changes nothing; Escape does not leave fullscreen there.


---

# Reference: wcs-* elements inside a React / Vue / Svelte / Solid app

<!-- source: wcstack-skill/skills/wcstack-app/references/frameworks.md -->

# wcs-* I/O nodes inside a React / Vue / Svelte / Solid app

Read this before putting a `wcs-*` element in a framework's component. Nothing here uses `data-wcs` or `@wcstack/state`: every I/O node implements wc-bindable, so a thin adapter (`@wc-bindable/react`, `/vue`, `/svelte`, `/solid`, …) maps an element's outputs into framework state with no per-element glue (`docs/framework-adapter-integration.md` in the wcstack repo). Worked apps: `examples/fw-inventory` (a React 19 back office and a Vue 3 panel, with an e2e spec) and `examples/websocket-chat` (React 19 and Vue 3 against the same server as the vanilla / state / signals variants).

The lint does not read a framework's components (it lists them under `not read:`): verify the app in the browser.

## The rules

1. **Use `@wc-bindable/*` 0.9 or later, and import the definition before the app renders anyway.** The adapters wait for a late definition (`syncOn: "define"`, their default) and bind when it lands; 0.8 and earlier checked once on mount and never retried, so an element that upgraded later stayed unbound with no error. A static import at the entry (`import "@wcstack/websocket/auto";` in `main.tsx`) works with every version. With a 0.8 adapter and a definition that arrives late (autoloader, CDN tag, code-split), gate the mount on `customElements.whenDefined("wcs-ws")`. A `syncOn` of your own replaces the default — keep `"define"` in it. `connectedCallbackPromise` covers connection, not definition.
2. **Pass object-valued inputs as properties, not attributes.** Attributes hold only strings, and several frameworks fall back to attributes when the property is not on the element yet, which stringifies the payload. Use `.prop` (Vue), `prop:` (Solid), `.prop=` (Lit), or assign through a ref. An element that finds an object written as an attribute when it connects (`files="[object File]"`) warns `[wcs/input-as-attribute]`. Assign a **new** object or array to change one: `files.push(f)` writes nothing a framework sees, and `body` / `files` are used up by each request.
3. **Pass deep plain copies of reactive store values.** Vue `reactive`, Svelte `$state`, Solid stores, MobX and Qwik `useStore` wrap objects in proxies, and a proxy cannot cross a structured-clone boundary — `<wcs-worker>` / `<wcs-broadcast>` report a `DataCloneError` into `error` instead of sending (and warn `[wcs/post-uncloneable]`). Vue's `toRaw()` unwraps **one level**: the rows of a reactive list are still proxies. Post `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(value))` (Vue, Qwik) or `$state.snapshot()` (Svelte).
4. **Read `event` outputs off the element, not the adapter's values.** `message` on `<wcs-sse>` / `<wcs-ws>` / `<wcs-broadcast>` / `<wcs-worker>` is an occurrence: through `values` + `useEffect` / `watch`, events that arrive together reach the component as one, and an equal value as none. Listen with `addEventListener("wcs-sse:message", …)` on the element; keep the adapter for `connected` / `loading` / `error` / a fetched `value`.
5. **Hold the element yourself, and call commands.** React's `useWcBindable` returns a callback ref and no element: wrap it (`const ref = useCallback((n) => { el.current = n; bindRef(n); }, [bindRef])`). In Vue `<script setup>`, name the template ref statically — `const { ref: socket, values } = useWcBindable()` + `<wcs-ws ref="socket">`; a `:ref="ref"` binding is unwrapped to `null` and the adapter never binds, with no warning. From framework state, call the command (`el.fetch()`, `el.upload()`, `el.save()`) instead of driving `trigger`: the element resets `trigger`, the framework still holds `true`, and the second `true` is never written.
6. **Mind the names and the order a framework uses.** React and Vue keep `key`: write `<wcs-storage storage-key="…">` (`key=` in JSX or a Vue template stores nothing). Props are applied in the order written, before the element is in the document: write the input that is read first first (an automatic `<wcs-upload>` keeps `files` that come before `url`). To follow another tab's `<wcs-storage>` from React, listen to `wcs-storage:value-changed` and skip the events your own save dispatches — applying the adapter's `value` back undoes the typing in between and loops. A component whose `key` changes remounts its I/O nodes (a new SSE connection each time); removing a prop does not close a stream — call `close()`.

## Around the rules

- Live handles such as `<wcs-camera>`'s `MediaStream` are not snapshot state — take them off the element's event via a ref.
- **Event names with a colon** (`wcs-fetch:response`): Angular templates cannot bind them; in React 19 JSX it depends on the transform (Babel refuses a namespaced name), and where it compiles the name is case-sensitive — `onwcs-fetch:response` works, `onWcs-fetch:response` never fires. `addEventListener` / `Renderer2.listen` is the portable path.
- **TypeScript**: every `/auto` entry has a type, so `import("@wcstack/sse/auto")` type-checks. JSX declarations for the tags are written by hand (`declare module "react" { namespace JSX { interface IntrinsicElements { "wcs-sse": … } } }`).
- **Vite's dev proxy**: end the response on a proxy error (`configure: (p) => p.on("error", (_e, _q, res) => res.destroy())`), or an SSE stream stays "connected" after the server restarts.


---

# Reference: verifying a page (the lint, wcs-schema / wcs-tsc, the console, DevTools, tests, SSR)

<!-- source: wcstack-skill/skills/wcstack-app/references/verification.md -->

# Verifying a wcstack page — the lint, the types, the console, tests, SSR

Read this before you declare a page finished. `SKILL.md` §5 holds the gate itself; this file holds how to run each check and how to read what it says.

## 1. The lint (`@wcstack/lint`, bin `wcs-validate`)

```bash
npx @wcstack/lint index.html                 # while authoring: warnings visible
npx @wcstack/lint --errors-only index.html   # the final gate, once every warning is fixed or explained
```

- **Pass every HTML file and every `wcstack.manifest.json` sidecar as separate arguments.** A `<wcs-state src="…">` file (`.json` / `.js` / `.ts`, a volume's too) is resolved relative to the HTML and read automatically — do not pass it. A `src` from `/` (`<wcs-state src="/app.js">` under `<base href="/ja/">`) is read only with `--root=<dir>`, the directory the server serves as `/`; a `src` the lint cannot read leaves that state unchecked and says so once (`wcs/state-src-unread`, info).
- **Each diagnostic names its code (`wcs/<code>`), a `source:line:col` range and the fix.** Fix every error and every actionable warning, then run it again. A warning can be a real defect — `wcs/binding-path-missing` is a column left empty, `wcs/event-token-unbound` a handler that never runs. The rules and what each means: the Diagnostics section of `packages/vscode-wcs/README.md` in the wcstack repo.
- **Severities follow the runtime**: what makes the runtime fail initialization or a binding is an error; what drops data silently is an error too (`wcs/nested-assign`, `wcs/array-mutation`, `wcs/storage-seed-clobber`, `wcs/input-nested-write`).
- **Files it did not check are named after the counts** — `not read:` for a framework's components and script files (`.jsx` / `.tsx` / `.vue` / `.svelte` / `.js` / `.ts`), `nothing to check:` for a page with no `data-wcs`, no `wcs-*` tag and no wcstack script. Exit `0` with those lines is not a verified page; a framework app is outside the gate — verify it in the browser.
- **Flags**: `--errors-only` (alias `--quiet`) hides warning and info lines but changes neither the counts nor the exit code. `--strict` exits `1` on warnings too — the right CI gate once every `<wcs-state src>` resolves and a `stateSchema` exists, since a path typo is otherwise only a warning; it combines with `--errors-only`. Exit `0` = no errors, `1` = errors, `2` = invalid usage or a file-read failure. `--lang=ja` / `--lang=en` force the message language.
- **Keep the lint at the page's version.** An older lint reports newer syntax as an error (`wcs/lint-version-behind` warns when the page pins a newer minor). 3.x pages stay on `@wcstack/lint@3.5` and the 1.21.x VS Code extension.
- An element marked `data-wcs-ignore` and its content are not checked. Under `$behavior: { enableMustache: false }` nothing about `{{ }}` is reported.

### What the analyzer reads, and what it cannot

- **List rows**: the analyzer follows `$listKeys` for list paths, and takes the row shape of a list that starts `[]` from the row literals in the assignments that add or replace rows anywhere in the script (`this.items.concat({ id, kind })`, `.toSpliced(i, n, { … })`, `.with(i, { … })`, `[...this.items, { … }]`, `this.rows = list.map((r) => ({ … }))`). A row passed as a variable (`concat(row)`) is invisible — inline the literal, or declare a `stateSchema`.
- **Data that arrives from outside** (`catalog: null` filled by `<wcs-fetch>` / `<wcs-storage>`) has no literal: declare its shape with JSDoc on the property — `/** @type {{ id: number, name: string }[] | null} */`, or a `@typedef` in the same script named there (a getter takes `@returns` or `@type`; a getter returning `this.catalog ?? []` keeps the shape).
- **A key written as a name** (`export default { lang, t }`, `items: ITEMS`) has the shape of the `const` or relative import it names. A key whose value is computed at run time (`team: init.team`, `errs: emptyErrs()`) leaves the paths under it unchecked, with one `wcs/path-dynamic-unknown` info: write the seed out as literals, or give the key a JSDoc `@type`.
- **A top-level spread in the state** (`export default { ...defaults(), … }`) hides the keys it brings in: without a `stateSchema` no path of that state is checked. Type the spread's expression (derive the type from the table: a JSDoc `@typedef` with a mapped type over `typeof TABLE`, the table marked `/** @type {const} */`, on the function's `@returns`).
- **The script rules** read what each getter, setter and method reads and writes of the state — the paths it reads or writes that the state lacks, a getter that writes, a setter that writes its own path or a path its getter does not read, a token emitted that nothing receives, a two-way binding on a getter without a setter, untracked reads. A relative path in a row accessor (`this[".name"]`) is read as the path under its row; a relative path in a method is not checked (its row is the caller's).
- **The lint does not see** `bootstrapXxx()` options, `#stop` / `stopPropagation()` around delegated handlers, elements your code moves, element writes used to reorder rows, `[data-wcs]` selectors, or SSR post-processing.

## 2. TypeScript

- **`wcs-schema` — check paths against the real types.** When the state is a TypeScript file (`<wcs-state src="./state.ts">`, or a build that emits `state.js` from it): `npx wcs-schema emit src/state.ts` (from `@wcstack/typescript`) writes `wcstack.manifest.json`, which the lint and the VS Code extension discover (the nearest one walking up from the HTML — do not pass it as an argument unless it should replace discovery). With a `stateSchema`, a path the type lacks is `wcs/path-nonexistent` (**error**) and `for:` on a non-array is `wcs/path-type-mismatch`; paths under a `Date` / `Map` / `Record<string, T>` stay silent. Gate CI with `npx wcs-schema check src/state.ts && npx wcs-validate --strict index.html`, and re-run `emit --merge` after changing the type (`--merge` replaces the named state wholesale; keep hand-written `stateSchema`s only for states you do not generate). A `state.js` works too — `wcs-schema` reads its JSDoc types. The regex analyzer cannot read `users: [] as { name: string }[]` without the schema. `emit` records the state file as `stateSource`, and the schema applies only to the pages whose root `<wcs-state src>` is that file: keep one `wcstack.manifest.json` at the root even when another page has an inline state of its own. A schema whose top-level keys differ from the script's is `wcs/drift-state-key` — regenerate it. Annotate getters' return types (`get total(): number {`); the lint reads them, and methods and `$watch` handlers may carry `: void`.
- **`wcs-tsc` — type-check the inline `<script type="module">` inside `<wcs-state>`** (npm + tsc projects): `npx wcs-tsc --noEmit` (optional peers `@volar/typescript@~2.4.0` + `@volar/language-core@~2.4.0`). The language plugin the VS Code extension uses gives `this` its type, wraps a bare `export default {}` in `defineState` and strips `@wcstack/state` imports, so `this.coutn++` fails as `index.html(9,14): error TS2551 … Did you mean 'count'?` — the write typo that would otherwise create a new key. The script is checked as JavaScript, as the browser runs it: type an inline state with JSDoc (`/** @type {Item[]} */ items: []`, `/** @typedef {import("./api").Item} Item */`), and TypeScript syntax (`const n: number`, `as`, `!`, `import type`) is an error — it would throw in the browser. A `$on` handler's parameters are typed (`state`, `event`, the indexes; `this` is an error) and `this.$command` has exactly the names in `$commandTokens`, in a `.ts` state through `defineState` too. The tsconfig must reach the pages (`include` covering them) and target ES2015+; use `strict`. `wcs-tsc` prints `wcs-tsc: warning: …` about what is missing — pages left out of the program included — and `--wcs-defaults` adds it to a temporary config. Other CDN imports are `any` (`--url-imports=error` to forbid). It checks the script side; the lint checks the HTML side — run both.
- **Building a `.ts` state (Vite).** `<wcs-state src="./src/state.ts">` works on the dev server, but `vite build` emits no state file without `wcstack()` from `@wcstack/typescript/vite` in `plugins`: production 404s the state. The plugin also keeps the inline scripts of `<wcs-state>` and `<wcs-guard-handler>` in the page (Vite takes them out). Without a bundler, compile with `tsc` and point `src` at the `.js`.
- **Both need `typescript` 5 or 6** (the peer is `>=5.0 <7`): install `typescript@6` — a bare `typescript` installs 7, which publishes no JavaScript compiler API.

## 3. The console

- **Every error the engine reports goes through `reportError()`**: a `<wcs-state>` that fails to initialize, a binding that fails to apply (with no `$errorCallback`), a getter / filter / handler / lifecycle callback / `$watch` handler that throws. `window.addEventListener("error", …)` receives each (the console shows it as uncaught; Playwright reports a `pageerror`), the original error as the `cause`. A state with `$errorCallback` sends its binding failures to the callback only — call `reportError(error)` inside it if a reporter must see them.
- **Messages carry the lint's code** (`[wcs/<code>]`), many with a number (`#501`). With the `diagnostics` feature (in `@wcstack/state` and `/auto`) they add the sentence, a did-you-mean and the replacement for a removed 3.x name; on `/core` without it they print `[wcs/<code>] #<number> <values>` — look the number up in the wcstack repo's `docs/state-errors.md`. A bracketed code means the lint reproduces the finding with a range: run it and fix every instance, not just the one that threw.
- **The diagnostics feature warns once about** a bound path that does not resolve, a path a getter reads that does not resolve, a write of an undeclared key beside a near one, a command token emitted while nothing subscribes, a delegated handler reading `currentTarget`, a `$on` handler that uses `this`, two root states, a bound element whose definition never comes, `data-wcs` on `<body>`, inserted markup left unbound, an I/O node's failure nothing reads. The check under-approximates on purpose — **no warning proves nothing**; only the lint checks exhaustively.
- **A `<wcs-state>` that fails to initialize** reports once (`#49`, with the element and its source) and rejects `connectedCallbackPromise`. Causes: a throwing or removed `$` declaration, a source that cannot load (`src="*.json"` HTTP error `#13`, `state="<id>"` with no JSON script of that id `#16`), a second root `<wcs-state>` (`#47`), and a page-level markup error (syntax, unknown filter, wildcard rank). `initializePromise` still resolves; `getBindingsReady(root)` rejects only when every `<wcs-state>` on that root failed before building its bindings; `setInitialState()` on a failed element throws (`#14` — replace the element). A `$connectedCallback` that throws after the bindings are built is `#50`: `connectedCallbackPromise` rejects, `getBindingsReady()` resolves.
- **Two messages point at the page, not at wcstack**: `render chain depth limit exceeded (100 drains …)` is a render loop — a row element's output, a `$renderedCallback` or a `$watch` keeps writing a new value into something the same render reads (`updates did not settle after 32 passes`, `#11`, is the same within one update); write only when the value really changes. `The host row of <x-row> was removed.` is a component's method or a kept `this` (a timer, a continuation after `await`) outliving its `for:` row — check the row is still there, and clear timers in `$disconnectedCallback`.
- **Every package's `bootstrapXxx(config)` throws on an option it does not have**; the lint cannot see those calls.

## 4. DevTools

When wiring is silent and the lint is clean, load `@wcstack/devtools/auto` (before state; on a split auto page add `devtools` to `features=`) and open the wiring pane's coverage view: declared against measured — `$watch` paths (fired ×N / never), command / event tokens (emitted ×N / never), bindings (attached / never attached). The closed badge counts the failures the runtime logged; a Wiring row whose path the runtime reported as unresolved carries an `unresolved` badge. Mount private keys appear only in the State pane's **Overlays** section. The overlay's shadow root is open: a test reads it through `document.querySelector("wcs-devtools").shadowRoot`. Its *prerequisite-missing* note on a row watch with no `for` and no `$listKeys` is a 3.x rule — under 4.0 such a watch fires (read it as "not fired yet").

## 5. Headless tests (npm projects)

A wcstack page is plain DOM: it tests under vitest + happy-dom with no browser, no test-only API and no build.

- **`@wcstack/testing`** (peers `@wcstack/state`, `@wcstack/server`): `const app = await mount(html)` registers the elements and waits for every element and binding (a `<wcs-router>`'s first route too — add `bootstrap: [async () => (await import("@wcstack/router")).bootstrapRouter()]`); a state in its own file mounts with `mount(html, { resolveModule })`. Then `app.state().write(s => …)` / `app.state().read(s => …)` (`app.state<typeof appState>()` types `s`), `fire(el, "click")`, `await settle()`, `app.unmount()`. It shims inline-script state loading, `textContent = 0` rendering as `""`, and happy-dom's parser moving a `<template>` out of a table (insert such markup yourself with `@wcstack/server`'s `setInnerHTML`, not `innerHTML`). Example suite: `examples/state-testing-todo/`.
- **Without the package**: setup file `bootstrapState(); URL.createObjectURL = undefined as any;` (routes the inline state through the `data:` loader — without it the state never finishes loading under Node). Test: `document.body.innerHTML = html` → `await stateEl.connectedCallbackPromise` → `await getBindingsReady(document)` → assert → `await stateEl.createStateAsync("writable", async (s) => { s.count = 42; })` (or `button.click()`) → `await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 0))` → assert. Write arrays reactively (`s.items = [...s.items, x]`). Bare Node: `installGlobals()` from `@wcstack/server`, then dynamic-import `@wcstack/state` after it. Details: `state-binding.md` §13.
- `renderToString()` from `@wcstack/server` gives a snapshot test.

## 6. Server rendering (`enable-ssr` + `@wcstack/server`'s `renderToString()`)

- Deploy `@wcstack/server` and the client at the same major.minor: the client discards a snapshot of another minor (3.x included) and renders the page itself. `@wcstack/server` depends on the `@wcstack/state` of its own version, so pinning the server pins the engine.
- Keep the HTML comments in the output — text bindings and row / branch markers are comments; a minifier's `removeComments` breaks hydration and lets `{{ }}` in values be read as bindings.
- Keep JSON values in SSR state (`Date` / `Set` / `Map` / class instances come back as strings or plain objects); derive the rest in getters.
- The render waits for a `<wcs-fetch>` whose url a binding set (within `timeoutMs`); a `<wcs-state src>` renders with `renderToString(html, { resolveModule })`; what the reader typed before hydration is kept. Details: `state-binding.md` §11, `router-and-scaffold.md` §5.

## 7. Serving and the browser

- A static single page needs no server (a tiny one if it fetches). An SPA needs the fallback "every extensionless non-API GET returns index.html" (`router-and-scaffold.md` §7).
- After the checks, run the page in a browser. Working references: `examples/` (multi-package demos) and `packages/*/examples/` (single-package demos) in the wcstack repo.
- In VS Code, the WcStack IntelliSense extension shows the lint's diagnostics inline, with hover, go-to-definition (F12 from a path into the state script), find-references and inlay hints. Other editors get `wcs-*` tag / attribute completion from its `wcs.html-data.json` under `html.customData`.


---

# Reference: a page pinned to an older 4.x release

<!-- source: wcstack-skill/skills/wcstack-app/references/versions.md -->

# A page pinned to an older 4.x release

`SKILL.md` and the other references describe the release named in `SKILL.md`'s `wcstack-version`. Read this only when the page pins an older 4.x release on its wcstack lines (`https://esm.run/@wcstack/state@4.9.0/auto`). For 3.x code, read `state-binding.md` §16 instead.

- **Keep the lint at the page's version** (`npx @wcstack/lint@4.9.0`). An older lint reports newer syntax as an error, and a newer lint reports rules the page's runtime does not follow.
- **Warnings arrive release by release.** The diagnostics warnings and lint rules this skill names may not exist at the page's version: silence there proves nothing. The checks themselves — the lint loop, the browser — still apply.
- **Upgrading instead**: `docs/upgrading-4x.md` in the wcstack repo lists, per release, what changes and which workarounds it makes unnecessary. Change only the versions, run the checks, then remove the workarounds one at a time — a workaround kept after its fix can fight it.

## What a pinned page writes differently

Each row applies to every release up to and including the one named. The workarounds are the ones the seam apps used, recorded in `docs/upgrading-4x.md`.

| Pinned at or below | What differs | Write instead |
|---|---|---|
| 4.27 | No loader for a DCC kept in a file; an eager key's loader is chosen by the key, never by the file's extension | A loader of the page's own that fetches the file and parses it with `setHTMLUnsafe()`, named in each eager key; or write the definition in every page |
| 4.27 | An element that writes when it is bound (`value#init=element:`) to a path under a volume whose file arrives after the root's throws `Path "…" does not exist`: the root fails and nothing is bound | Bind the element to a root key and copy it to and from the volume by `$watch` |
| 4.27 | A DCC's `$connectedCallback` sees the default, not the first value the page gives; an attribute on a DCC is ignored without a word; `#ro` on one mapped key does not hold for a component mounted inside | Derive from the input in a getter; bind every input; do not rely on `#ro` across two levels |
| 4.27 | A wrong name between a page and a mounted component is silent on both sides; a volume's mount path and a component writing its mounted tree can warn `[wcs/write-path-missing]` falsely | Unit-test the component with the page's data; ignore that message for a mount path |
| 4.27 | `mount()` (`@wcstack/testing`) never defines a DCC written in the HTML; `wcs-schema check` on a root with merged volumes always fails | Define the part by hand before `mount()`; run `check` for the volumes only |
| 4.26 | An `eventToken.*`, an output-property binding or a `bindNode` signal also hears a nested element's bubbling event of the same name, with the inner element's `detail` | Check `event.target` in the handler, or do not nest two elements of the same kind |
| 4.26 | A form the router draws before the root state loads can be submitted natively — a GET with the fields, a password too, in the URL — and text typed before binding is erased | Write `disabled` on the submit button in the markup and bind it (`disabled: sending`), so it is usable only once bound |
| 4.25 | Clearing `<wcs-sse>` / `<wcs-ws>`'s `url` leaves the connection open; `<wcs-sse>` does nothing when the page leaves | Call `close()` with clearing `url` (sign-out); close the stream in a `beforeunload` listener only on a page without a router (WebKit fires it on router navigations) |
| 4.25 | `<wcs-debounce>` / `<wcs-throttle>` `value` starts `undefined` and seeds the bound slot with it | Guard the slot's `$watch` against `undefined` |
| 4.25 | No Vite plugin; `wcs-tsc` checks an inline state as TypeScript (JSDoc ignored, a type annotation passes) | Mark inline scripts `vite-ignore` and emit the `src` state file yourself; write an inline state without annotations |
| 4.24 | The screen and sensor elements have no `supported` output, and `<wcs-permission>` no `unsupportedReason` | Detect the API yourself (`document.fullscreenEnabled`, `"share" in navigator`, `document.permissionsPolicy`) before offering the button |
| 4.24 | `<wcs-tilt>` sets `permissionState` to `"denied"` when an iPhone refused to ask (a call outside a tap), and has no `heading` | Read `"denied"` with a non-null `error` as "not asked yet" (`permissionState !== "granted"` shows the button); find north with a `deviceorientationabsolute` / `webkitCompassHeading` listener |
| 4.24 | `<wcs-accelerometer>` / `<wcs-gyroscope>` are `unsupported` where the browser has no sensor class (an iPhone, Firefox) | A `devicemotion` listener of the page's own, with `DeviceMotionEvent.requestPermission()` called from the tap |
| 4.24 | `<wcs-credential>` has no `preventSilentAccess` and does not build a `PasswordCredential`; `<wcs-contacts>` writes `value: []` when the picker is closed | Call `navigator.credentials.preventSilentAccess()` on sign-out and build `new PasswordCredential(…)` for `store()`; read an empty array as "closed" |
| 4.24 | `<wcs-ws>`'s `close` and `<wcs-idle>`'s `start` wired straight to a button (`onclick: $command.close`) take the event as their first argument and fail | Emit them from a state method with no arguments |
| 4.24 | `<wcs-fullscreen>` / `<wcs-pointer-lock>` / `<wcs-pip>` keep `active: true` after they leave the document | Write the flag back to `false` when the route that holds them is left |
| 4.24.1 | A route's static segment is a regular expression (`/v1.0` matches `/v1x0`), a path with characters outside ASCII matches no URL, and `params` arrive percent-encoded | Keep route paths to ASCII and avoid `.`, `+` and brackets (or write the path percent-encoded); decode a param by hand. From 4.24.2 params arrive decoded — decoding again throws for a value with a `%` |
| 4.23 | A button **beside** a `<wcs-link>` in a `for:` row runs no handler, or its neighbour's; `to: .href` (a property binding) leaves the `<a>` with no `href` | A plain `<a>` in the row in place of `<wcs-link>`; `attr.to: .href` |
| 4.23 | `<wcs-fetch>`'s `fetch` command ignores its arguments; `<wcs-infinite-scroll>` stops while its sentinel stays on screen after a short page | Write the url first and emit `fetch` from a `$watch` on it; give the target a static `url` for page 1, and make pages large enough to push the sentinel out of the window |
| 4.23 | `data-wcs` on `<body>` / `<html>` and an `on*:` on `<wcs-link>` do nothing, with no warning | The same on every version: bind on an element inside `<body>`, and put handlers inside or around the link |
| 4.23 | The lint reads only the first `@typedef` of a JSDoc block | One `@typedef` per block |
| 4.22 | No `forms` add-on: state writes into a field while it is composed with an IME, a value the browser fills without an `input` event (a password manager) never reaches state, and a reset blanks the fields while state keeps its values | Bind a field that normalizes what is typed one way and write it from a handler that skips `event.isComposing`; a `change` listener that copies the field into state; a `clear()` method that assigns state instead of `type="reset"` |
| 4.22 | An I/O element in a `for:` row that is reordered aborts its request (or restarts its timer) when the row moves | Do not reorder rows while a row's request is in flight |
| 4.21 | No relative paths in script (`this[".name"]`) and no accessor declared for several lists (`get "a.*.x,b.*.x"()`) | The same accessor body written once per list with full paths, repeated under a filtered copy (`get "shown.*.fullName"()` beside `get "users.*.fullName"()`) |
| 4.19 | Every `<wcs-state src>` naming one module gets the same state object (a DCC's or a component's instances share it); the number filters (`locale`, `currency`, `toFixed`, …) refuse an absent value | Export a factory and build each state in an inline module; `\|coalesce(0)` in front of `locale` where the value can be absent |
| 4.16 | A setter that writes its own path overflows the stack with a `RangeError` naming nothing; a setter whose getter does not read what it writes is not reported | The rules are the same (store under a key the getter reads); only the messages are missing |
| 4.15 | No `$update(path, indexes, fn)`; a `$setAll` mapper is not run at the row it writes | Read and write the row path: ``const p = `items.${i}.label`; this[p] = this[p] + " !!!";`` |
| 4.11 | `<wcs-link>` has no `query-keys`: over a paged list, a tab is current on page 1 only | Plain `<a>` tabs with `attr.aria-current:` from state |
| 4.10.1 | A `<wcs-link to="/notices">` (no query) is current on every query | Plain `<a>` with its own `aria-current` |
| 4.9 | A link to a bare fragment (`<a href="#main">`, a skip link) under `<base href>` goes to the home route; a `<wcs-link>` with a query is current everywhere; under `<wcs-view-transition>` a `$watch` runs before the transition's bindings; the date filters take no time zone | An `onclick#prevent:` handler that focuses `#main`; plain `<a>` with `attr.aria-current:` and `class.…:` bindings; navigation and focus moves in `$renderedCallback`; `Intl.DateTimeFormat(…, { timeZone })` in getters |
| 4.8 | `leaveConfirm` on `<wcs-router>` turns a boolean into the question's text (`confirm("false")`); `<wcs-upload>` sends no request header; `<wcs-sse>` stays closed after the browser gives up; `@wcstack/testing`'s `mount()` cannot load a `<wcs-state src>` | Bind a string or `null` (`get discardPrompt() { return this.dirty ? "…" : null; }`); `UploadCore` imported from the CDN and driven from state; a timer that reopens the stream on `errorInfo.recoverable === false`; a copy of the state in an inline script for the test |
| 4.7 | No `stale-after` on `<wcs-sse>` / `<wcs-ws>`; an open `<wcs-ws>` keeps the page out of the back/forward cache | A watchdog of the page's own (the time of the last message, a close and a reopen after a silence); close the socket in `pagehide`, open it in `pageshow` |
| 4.6 | The engine's errors reach `console.error` only, not `window`'s `error` event; a date filter refuses `null` | An `$errorCallback` that calls `reportError()`; an `if:` around a date binding whose value arrives later |
| 4.5 | `<wcs-storage>` has no `storage-key` (React / Vue keep `key`); an automatic `<wcs-upload>` drops `files` written before `url`; no `/auto` entry has a type | `el.key = …` through a ref; `url` before `files`; a declaration of your own (`declare module "@wcstack/*/auto";`) |
| 4.4 | A disconnect does not publish what it changes (a route left with `<wcs-camera>` in it still says the camera is on); a feature the page cannot use looks like the user's refusal | A `$watch` on `routeName` that writes `active` / `recording` back to `false`; read `document.permissionsPolicy` and `isSecureContext` yourself |
| 4.2 | No `data-wcs-ignore`: every `{{ }}`, `data-wcs` and comment binding in the page is read; `<wcs-fetch>` skips a url equal to the last one fetched even after an empty url in between | Never put markup you did not write into the page; `manual` on the read `<wcs-fetch>` and a `$watch` on its url that emits a `fetch` command |
| 4.1 | No date styles or `currency` on the filters | `Intl.DateTimeFormat` / `Intl.NumberFormat` formatters in getters |
| 4.0.4 | `$watch` does not fire for a value the router or an open stream already has at load; no `leaveConfirm`; `<wcs-link>` has no `match="prefix"`; `value:` on `<wcs-fetch-header>` sends an empty header | The same work in `$connectedCallback`; a `navigate` listener of the page's own; the section link's mark computed by the page; `attr.value:` on the header |
